Troubleshooting Spellwork

If your spell did not produce the intended results, many factors could have contributed. Before declaring it null, wait for at least a full lunar cycle (twenty-eight days) for the intention to come to pass.

Doubt

Doubt is the killer of all magick. The fastest way to make sure your magick will not come to pass is to doubt that it will. The power comes from you, not the candles, incense, or chants. If you think you do not have the oomph needed, do not doubt. Work it out.

Lack of Power

When casting your intention and putting your spell out into the ether, you have to feel it in your bones. If it feels like you are reciting your phone number for a telemarketer, you are not going to have the desired results. Sound off like you mean it.

Speaking of meaning it, stop and take stock to make sure this is something you really want. It could be that the reason a workable amount of energy cannot be raised is that it is not a sincere desire.

Patience

It takes time for magick to work. Sometimes your working works right away, but that happens less often than you might think, and frequently only after a lot of practice. Magick is a skill, no matter how many witches you see in movies and television discovering they are magickal and knowing everything within two minutes.

Take a deep breath and know your intention is working.

Shoddy Scholarship

There is a reason that witches and even faerie tale wizards are associated with books. Knowledge is power, and without the know-how, your magick is not going to get any wind in its sails. Take the time to do the research needed to feel supported and fulfilled in your magickal endeavors. After all, you are building your magickal intent and your brain.

Lack of Focus

If your magick does not have a specific outcome, it scatters your attention, and therefore your intention. If your original plan is "Money for a new car" and mid-spell you start thinking how nice it would be to have some new clothes, but then you would have to work more hours, to pay for the clothes, and you really should get a new job because you are miserable here, and your boss is difficult... Do you see how that can take the fire out of the spell?

Concentrate while you are working and find a friend to vent to later. The same goes for trying to cast a spell in a house full of people, or in a messy room. All of these things can scatter your focus.

Too Many Cooks in the Kitchen

Working magick with friends and loved ones is fun. It can bring people closer together and is an excellent way to bond. However, bringing a friend, loved one, or partner into your magickal practice should be done carefully, if at all.

The idea of a coven sounds scintillating and neat. However, having a new practitioner who may or may not have a clear picture of what to do or how to do it can break down the building energy. Not to mention, if your spell is for a new car and your best friend thinks you need a sensible older model and to pay down your debt, it can break down the momentum you were gaining doing all the research.

If you want to practice with magickal friends, keep it simple and make sure everyone is on the same page.

Volatile Emotions

If you are too upset to drive, or crying too hard to talk, those emotions can hinder your magickal practice. This is not about mental health. Telling people they have to be 100 percent mentally healthy before someone will love them is harmful and ableist.

This is about giving yourself time to collect your thoughts and feelings, wipe the tears away, and ground yourself. This makes for a more focused intent. Trying to work magick when emotional can lead to overextended energy and unfocused, drained results.

By properly grounding before spell work, the practitioner ensures connection to the earth and a well of energy.

The Witches' Pyramid

To Know, To Will, To Dare, To Keep Silent.

These four pillars support effective magickal practice:

  • To Know: Do your research. Understand your correspondences, timing, and methods.
  • To Will: Commit fully. Your intention must be sincere and your focus unwavering.
  • To Dare: Take action. Magick requires courage to step into the unknown.
  • To Keep Silent: Protect your working. Sharing too soon can introduce doubt and scatter energy.

Why Do Some Spells Succeed but Others Fail?

Magick works. It can produce outcomes so unexpected and wonderful they might almost be called miracles. And yet, magick does not work every time. Even skilled practitioners face challenges and experience failure. Learning to work magick does not shield anyone from all disappointment.

A well-known herbalist, sought out by patients from around the world, once framed this plainly for her students: roughly a third of the remedies she prescribed failed outright. Another third produced only modest improvement. The final third produced extraordinary results. Her lesson was direct: as a healer, you must get over your fear of failure. If the first remedy does not work, try another, rather than deciding the situation is hopeless and giving up.

It Comes Down to Clarity

Successful magick does not require arcane techniques, expensive ingredients, or complicated rituals. Often, what separates a working that succeeds from one that fails is clarity of intention.

Consider a practitioner who had spent years searching for love without pausing to feel what their soul actually needed. Through meditation, they identified three specific qualities they truly wanted in a partner, not what seemed reasonable, not what they thought they deserved, but what they genuinely needed. They wrote those three things on a page torn from a book of love poetry and burned a candle over the petition. Simple, honest, and precise. Weeks later, they encountered the first partner who met all three criteria.

The spell worked not because of its complexity, but because of its honesty.

Asking for What You Actually Want

Knowing what you truly want is difficult. Asking for it can be even harder.

Kasia Urbaniak, a coach who draws on her background as a dominatrix to teach people about power dynamics in personal and professional life, has observed that many people, particularly women, avoid asking for what they want. Even when the desire is known, the request gets internally compromised before it is voiced. Instead of asking for what is truly wanted, people ask for what they think they deserve. The result: even when the request is granted, the outcome feels hollow, because it was not what was really wanted in the first place.

This applies directly to spellwork. A spell cast toward a compromised desire rather than the true desire will succeed in delivering something that still disappoints.

Close your eyes and take a breath. What do you really want?

Ancestral Trauma as a Block to Magick

The internal voice that forces self-compromise before a request is made is often a symptom of ancestral trauma. Someone in the ancestral line experienced pain, loss, or discrimination and developed a coping mechanism that helped them survive, but which now limits their descendants' ability to thrive. Sometimes this person was known in life; sometimes their name has been lost to living memory entirely.

One common pattern involves career and livelihood. Ancestors who survived under conditions of severe employment discrimination often passed down advice centered on keeping a low profile, not making waves, and never complaining. This wisdom served its original context. But in a professional environment where asking for what one deserves is standard practice, this inherited coping strategy can actively work against success. A practitioner might cast spell after spell for a promotion and see nothing manifest, not because the spell is weak, but because the ancestral pattern underneath it is running a counter-program.

The work in cases like this begins at the ancestor altar. Opening up to the ancestors honestly, naming the fear and the inherited pattern, and asking for their help in releasing it, can dissolve a block that no amount of spellwork alone would touch. When that inner preparation is complete, the spell that follows can manifest with unusual speed.

Close your eyes and take a breath. Who told you that you couldn't have what you really want?

The Real Magick Is in the Preparation

Sometimes the most important magick is the preparation done to become capable of receiving what is being asked for.

This can mean healing ancestral trauma. It can also mean developing the skills, experience, and readiness required to steward what is being sought. New jobs, new relationships, and increased abundance all require more of the person who receives them. Clearing the inner ground is not a detour from the work. It is often the work itself.

Recognizing Magickal Attack

Understanding the sources of magickal attack and crossed conditions enables proper diagnosis and response. Attack rarely appears from nowhere. Recognizing its origin allows you to select appropriate protective measures and remedies.

Before You Assume You're Cursed

True curses are rare. They require time, attention, effort, and often specialized supplies and a knowledgeable practitioner. Most people who fear they've been cursed are simply experiencing a run of bad luck, which can be addressed through refreshing protections.

Own your magick. Your magick belongs to you alone. Don't give it away by telling yourself you've been cursed. Stand in your power and recognize your strength. Laugh (yes, really) in the face of the mere idea of a curse. Laughter carries sound waves of joy and mirth. By directing laughter at a potential curse, you've already defeated nine out of ten magickal threats. Jinxes especially, being small things devoid of true intention, crumble against genuine mirth.

Ask yourself: Who would want to curse me? Hopefully the answer is simple. Most practitioners have one or two people they've argued with, but these are usually minor threats. If you have a long list of people who hate you enough to hex you, it's time to re-evaluate. What do these people have in common? If they're all social media conflicts, consider whether that's where your time is best spent. If they're people you've wronged, honesty is the only path forward. If they're people whose boundaries you've maintained, good for you. The only people who hate healthy boundaries are those who benefit from your lack of them.

Curse Threat Assessment

Check all that apply:

  • ☐ A run of bad luck
  • ☐ Unexplained pain
  • ☐ Perception of soul loss or soul theft
  • ☐ A perception of people talking about you, especially disembodied voices
  • ☐ Sudden clumsiness
  • ☐ Feelings of someone standing on your chest or arms
  • ☐ Being run-down without cause
  • ☐ Nightmares out of the ordinary
  • ☐ Feelings of being watched or followed

Grading Your Assessment

1-3 checks: Bad luck or anxiety. Refresh your home's warding and protections. Vary your cleansing methods on a regular schedule: asperge with full moon water and a pine branch one month, bang pots and pans together the next, burn mugwort the month after. Varying practice prevents the magickal equivalent of a resistant infection, keeps your methods unpredictable, and accounts for the fact that friends don't always stay in your life forever.

4-6 checks: Possible jinx. A salt bath or shower blessing wouldn't hurt. Sound is excellent for cleansing: bells, tuning forks, or loud music all help. Layer your home protections with three, six, or nine different types of magickal barriers. No single method is proof against all threats.

7-9 checks: Possible curse or hex. Cleanse yourself first with herbal washes or waters, then cleanse your home several times using different methods in logical order (smoke before floor wash, so you can clean any ash). Leave offerings for your house spirit: coffee, bread, porridge, or wine. They are your first line of defense, but they need relationship. A cup of coffee weekly can save you a lot in repair bills.

10 checks: Seek professional help. This is too much for one person. Therapeutic and magickal interventions go hand in hand. Seek recommendations for an ethical practitioner from a trusted friend or local metaphysical shop.

Four Primary Sources

Occult attack and crossed conditions generally stem from one of four sources, each requiring different approaches to resolution.

1. Offended Spirits

Humans share this planet with numerous spiritual beings and intelligences. All space carries awareness and energy. Through thoughtless actions that disturb the natural environment, practitioners risk upsetting these spirits and earning their wrath.

Common offenses include burning and dumping waste, damming rivers and lakes, building in sacred spaces, and other disruptions to natural environments. These spirits exist as energy and awareness, affecting people on subtle layers that filter into physical symptoms through the immune and nervous systems. They also influence emotional disposition and thought processes.

Traditional medicine and shamanism across cultures address maladies caused by these spirits. Resolution typically requires:

  • Treating physical symptoms
  • Exorcising the offending spirits
  • Making appropriate offerings
  • Asking forgiveness from the spirits

2. Places of Power

Locations carrying concentrated spiritual energy or housing powerful entities can harm the unprepared. Modern life has dulled most people's psychic sensitivity, allowing them to pass through such places unaffected. However, those with even slight sensitivity may experience sudden, overwhelming amplification of awareness when entering these spaces, leaving them vulnerable to forces they never knew existed.

Naturally powerful sites include ley-line nexuses and fairy mounds where geo-psychic energy gathers.

Human-empowered sites include ancient shrines, graveyards, or locations where psychically potent events occurred: murder, assault, or even séances performed long ago.

Even benign powers can overwhelm someone unprepared for the shift in perception. These places can ignite latent psychic potential without warning, creating shock and vulnerability.

Risk for practitioners: Occultists who regularly work with unseen forces encounter these dangers more frequently than ordinary people. Even common practices like casting circles, scrying, divining, and raising power illuminate the astral plane and attract attention from subtle realm inhabitants. Advanced experimental work increases risk, but even basic practices can cause problems for some people, particularly those with existing emotional or mental health challenges.

3. Missteps in Practice

Broken vows, improper ritual closure, neglected obligations to spirits, or other errors in occult practice create openings for negative consequences. This category includes:

  • Broken promises to deities or spirits
  • Abandoned workings left incomplete
  • Violated taboos within specific traditions
  • Improper handling of spiritual contracts
  • Failed protective measures during dangerous work

These attacks stem not from external malice but from the practitioner's own errors creating vulnerability or invoking natural consequences.

Broken vows deserve special attention. Promises made during initiations, self-empowerment ceremonies, or solitary vows to gods and spirits will rebound if broken. When vows invoke powerful guardians of a coven or magickal order, breaking them can escalate from simple crossed conditions to full attacks from the very guardians that once protected you. Symptoms include spells ceasing to work and noticeable loss of vitality.

Resolution requires creating a rite of apology and offering, potentially renouncing the vow if it cannot be kept. Be discerning about what you agree to before making spiritual commitments.

4. Attacks from Other Practitioners

Deliberate magickal assault from another person represents the most commonly feared but least common source. Despite claims that "real" witches never harm others or that karma prevents magicians from cursing, history and practice prove otherwise. Curses and bindings have always been part of witchcraft, from Greek defixiones tablets to traditional rootwork to modern practitioners worldwide.

Reality of harmful magick: Most practitioners apply the same ethical standards to magick as to other actions. If they would take mundane revenge or influence, they may use magick for the same ends. Even self-identified "white lighters" sometimes curse when they believe their cause is just. Items for harmful and coercive magick remain popular in occult shops.

Professional curse work: Practitioners can be hired to send curses, though many workers refuse such jobs without good cause. In traditional cultures, approaching a witch for both cursing and uncrossing work was common practice.

Unintentional attacks: Not all harmful magick is deliberate. Gifted individuals can manifest powerful hexes without training or intent through sheer emotional charge. The Italian Maloccio (evil eye) operates through envy, hatred, or ill-wishing. People with weak constitution can become psychic parasites, unintentionally draining vitality from those around them. These accidental attacks still require attention and remedy.

Signs include sudden and inexplicable misfortune coinciding with conflict with another practitioner, patterns of bad luck that feel targeted rather than random, or direct threats made by someone with magickal knowledge.

Diagnosis

Proper diagnosis requires honest assessment:

Consider timing: When did symptoms begin? What preceded them?

Examine your actions: Have you disturbed natural spaces, broken spiritual commitments, or come into conflict with practitioners?

Assess the pattern: Does misfortune feel random or targeted? Does it affect specific life areas or manifest as general malaise?

Rule out mundane causes: Physical illness, mental health conditions, and ordinary bad luck account for most perceived attacks. Consult appropriate medical and mental health professionals first.

Response Framework

Once you identify the source, select remedies that address the specific type of attack:

For offended spirits: Offerings, apologies, exorcism, and behavior correction

For places of power: Cleansing, grounding, protective boundaries, and avoiding the location

For practice missteps: Fulfilling obligations, closing workings properly, making amends to spirits, and correcting technique

For practitioner attacks: Protective workings, reversals, binding, and direct confrontation when necessary

Many protective rituals in this grimoire specify which sources they address. Select workings appropriate to your situation rather than applying general protection indiscriminately.

Identifying Attack

Regular banishing rituals and protections prevent most problems. Vigilant practice strengthens mind and spirit while shielding against unwanted influences. However, no protection is foolproof. Attacks, accidental or intentional, sometimes breach defenses and affect health, luck, and wellbeing. Recognizing attack when it occurs is the first step to combating it.

The Denial Problem

People resist admitting attack is happening. Non-practitioners may fear they are losing their minds rather than acknowledge occult causes. Even suspecting magickal reasons, they avoid speaking up to prevent being labeled mentally unbalanced.

Even magicians struggle to admit vulnerability. Many overestimate their abilities or believe their protections are infallible. Ego makes it difficult to admit something got through defenses. This proves especially challenging for teachers and leaders who fear losing credibility by appearing vulnerable.

Two key principles:

  1. No one is impervious to psychic attack. Basic protections defend against most accidental attacks and general malefic energy, even most intentional attacks, but no technique is foolproof regardless of initiation level or perceived power.
  2. No harm comes from defending against an attack that may not be happening, but great harm comes from ignoring a real attack. Play it safe.

Psychic Hypochondriacs

Some people convince themselves they are constantly under attack with no basis in reality. These individuals create drama through "psychic soap operas" and seek help repeatedly.

An inverse relationship exists between insistence someone is being attacked and the probability they actually are. These folks claim persecution from unknown "black lodges" and "dark magicians" with no motive beyond pure evil.

When encountering these patterns, offer simple cleansing or shielding instructions and perhaps an amulet. When they return repeatedly, gently decline by performing divination and stating you cannot detect the source of attack. This avoids contradicting their beliefs while establishing you cannot help.

Symptoms of Attack

Spiritual attack manifests in three categories: external conditions, mental conditions, and physical conditions.

External Conditions: Crossed Conditions

These attacks affect probability and luck, creating "crossed conditions." Early signs include:

  • Feeling out of step with time
  • Chronic lateness despite efforts
  • Patterns of bad luck
  • Everything touched going wrong
  • Multiple mishaps in short timeframes (several car incidents within days)
  • Objects breaking or falling when handled
  • People losing patience with you
  • Unexpected bills piling up
  • Inability to hold onto money

Left untreated, symptoms escalate: job loss, relationship dissolution, car accidents, false accusations, potential jail time. Severity depends on the attacker's power and how long conditions persist.

Each incident has rational material explanation. Taken alone, they mean nothing. Together, a string of unfortunate coincidences indicates something is wrong, especially when accompanied by mental and physical symptoms.

Mental Conditions

Most magickal and psychic attacks produce mental symptoms in targets. While suggestion is powerful and can manifest symptoms, genuine magickal attacks typically remain secret. True attackers do not tip off their targets.

Common mental symptoms:

  • Despair, oppression, anxiety, and fear without identifiable cause
  • Inexplicable confusion or inability to focus
  • Troubled dreams
  • Feeling constantly followed
  • Hearing voices when alone
  • Seeing shadows and outlines of things that are not there
  • Smelling scents without source (sulfur or rot can indicate attack)

Coercive attacks: Telepathic attacks, hypnotic attacks, and coercive magick aimed at influencing actions rather than causing harm produce primarily mental effects. These manifest as:

  • Uncharacteristic compulsions
  • New affinities or aversions
  • Acting out of character

The mind justifies these feelings as natural, making self-recognition difficult. If friends and loved ones report you are acting strangely, consider their observations seriously. Normal influence operates like ringing a doorbell from outside, attack operates like lifting floorboards and pulling the bell wires directly.

Important medical note: Many mental attack symptoms overlap with depression, schizophrenia, anxiety, ADHD, and other psychological conditions. Magickal defenses should NOT substitute for therapy and psychological treatment. These methods may be used alongside conventional treatment but must never replace medical care.

Physical Conditions

Physical symptoms can accompany attacks. Always seek medical attention for physical symptoms. Treat the symptom medically while occult defense addresses the cause.

Common physical symptoms:

Headaches: Early warning sign, especially when the scalp feels stretched too thin over the skull. When lying down, aches may gather to one side indicating the direction of attack.

Fatigue: Second most common indicator, particularly in parasitic and vampiric attacks.

  • Parasitic attacks: Someone with weak constitution unintentionally drains higher vitality from others, common between family members or close friends, especially in caregiver relationships ("the caregiver goes first")
  • Living vampires: Intentional drawing of vitality from others to add to their own power
  • Undead vampires: Spirits that have fought off astral decay and sustain themselves by feeding on the living, leaving microscopic wounds
  • Expedition Mort: Haitian Vodou curse where the target is handed to the dead. Something personal is placed in a willing spirit's grave, and grave dirt is planted on target or home. Creates terrible fatigue and troubled, unrestful sleep that can lead to death if untreated.

Weight on chest while sleeping: Called "Hag Riding," the most common complaint when spirits attack or haunt. Sometimes accompanied by feelings of sexual aggression. Unexplained bruises can develop from nighttime attacks.

Sudden persistent illness: From simple flu to cancer to undiagnosable conditions, curses affect the physical body directly. In rare cases of powerful attacks, heart attacks and aneurysms can result.

Sexual dysfunction: Loss of interest and impotency from jinxes by jealous or jilted lovers. Folk magick worldwide contains spells for removing and restoring "sexual nature."

Digestive issues: Stopped bowels are a traditional attack form found in grimoires like Albertus Magnus's Egyptian Secrets and the Icelandic Galdrabok.

Omens and Early Warnings

Beyond direct symptoms, watch for warning signs:

Dreams

The deep mind communicates through dreams. Rather than relying on dream dictionaries (each person has their own symbol set), assess overall content and character:

  • Were you being persecuted or pursued?
  • Were loved ones turning away?
  • Did you feel trapped?

Watch your dreams if you suspect attack. Talented oneiric practitioners can sometimes divine the attacker's name from dreams.

Animal Behavior and Omens

  • How do animals react to you?
  • Are you encountering more chthonic creatures (spiders, snakes)?
  • Have animals died in your yard?
  • Strange animal occurrences signal potential attack

Early Warning Systems

Plants: Keep live plants in each room. Under magickal attack, plants suffer first and will be affected before you are.

Silver: Keep silver in your shoe and around your neck (silver dimes with holes are traditional in the southern United States). Silver turns black under attack due to sulfur in curse powders like Goofer Dust.

Fresh egg on altar: Indicates and absorbs attack. Eggs go bad quickly or break under negative energy.

Amulets: When protective amulets break or get lost, their protection has been breached. Broken amulet cords signal attack.

Cooper's Color Code for Awareness

Col. Jeff Cooper developed a code of awareness that helps explain mental readiness in response to a threat, and how each scenario should affect it. This framework applies equally well to magickal threats as physical ones.

Code White - Completely unaware of your surroundings, unable to respond to a threat. This includes being asleep in your bed at home, texting, walking with head down, being lost in thought, and others.

Code Yellow - Aware of your surroundings, but not worried about any specific threat to your person. Engaged with your surroundings.

Code Orange - You've been alerted to a specific threat: this could be a car coming toward you, an angry dog coming your way, or a person invading your space in a threatening manner. Formulate your response now, before it's a threat to you.

Code Red - Immediate danger, requires active response. This could be running away, yelling, fighting, or more. Implement the plan you came up with in the previous step.

Code Black - This is a freeze response, and it is totally normal to freeze when faced with a potential threat. There is no shame in this. However, it is a learning experience. The way to train out of a freeze response is through practice. If you can go over scenarios in your mind while out and about, it can help you plan your moves ahead of time. Remember, action is always faster than reaction.

Candle Magick for Each Awareness Level

Use Cooper's color code to do some candle magick for your protection.

White - Burn a white candle anointed with diluted anise oil to light the way for pleasant dreams, the best time to be unaware of your surroundings.

Yellow - Empower a yellow candle on a Sunday with sunflower oil to alert you to magickal threats; think an early warning system. Repeat anytime you suspect something afoot.

Orange - In color magick, orange is a combination of yellow (air/thought) and red (fire/action). Use an orange candle on a Wednesday (to speed action) to spur you into action to protect yourself, family, or home.

Red - Anoint on a Tuesday with jojoba (removes obstacles) to give you the strength needed to fight back. Add a pinch of cumin for some Mars fire.

Black - Burn a black candle on a Saturday (endings) to ward off a freeze response in stressful situations. Journal responses to threats so your brain knows what to do instead.

Important Perspective

Taken individually, every symptom has a logical mundane explanation. When many symptoms and events occur within a short time, this indicates genuine attack. Err on the side of caution. Do not ignore symptoms when they occur.

Reversals and Counter-Magick

If you are vigilant in your banishings, use protective amulets, and have strong guardians, even if someone were to lay a curse directly on you, it is likely that you would not even notice. The entire attack will roll off you or be sent back to the sender automatically. There can be times, however, when normal defenses do not hold, and a more active position must be assumed to ensure the wellbeing of you and your loved ones. Thus far this page has dealt only with strictly pacifying, protective, and preventative measures. Under the majority of circumstances, these will be all that is needed. Unfortunately, in some cases, an obsessive enemy will show no sign of stopping their harassment, and you will need to resort to more heavy-handed methods to ensure successful defense. For this reason, it is important to master the techniques of reversal and counter-magick.

The Law of Three

There is a well-known axiom that has entered Wicca known as the Law of Three. This law is typically interpreted as a sort of amplified karma and states that any harm done by the witch will come back upon them three times over. According to some contacts in traditional craft, the original meaning of the Law of Three is different. The idea was that if a witch is harmed or cursed that they should send it back to the offender three times over. This ensures that the enemy, should they survive the triple reversal, will not attempt the same foolishness again. As this grimoire focuses on defense, the emphasis here is not on sending things back "three times over." It is, however, sometimes a good idea to reverse an attack upon the attacker, forcing them to fall into a trap of their own making.

Identifying Your Attacker

Though it's not always necessary, it is beneficial if you know who it is that you are reversing a curse back upon. Unfortunately, this is not always possible. While some less-adept sorcerers rely on the psychological power of someone knowing they have been cursed as part of the curse itself, a truly powerful witch will not reveal their identity, allowing the curse to work in secret. If your enemy has not shown their hand by pointing dramatically and pronouncing a curse verbally, they may have left evidence in the form of physical objects used to deliver the curse to you.

Physical Evidence:

  • Powders such as Goofer Dust and Graveyard Dust are common, as are condition powders such as Bend Over, Crossing, Commanding, and Black Arts
  • These powders are usually laid in places where you will come into contact with them or step on them, such as on the doorstep, in the car, or even on paper that is mailed to you
  • Items such as gris-gris bags, jack balls, and paper talismans can be placed in or around your home or office to deliver power to you
  • If any of these or other suspect items are found, they can be gathered and used to hone your reversal spells on the correct sender

Personal Links:

If there are no items you can find, perhaps the offender has collected something of yours to use as a link. Think about:

  • People who have been guests and used your bathroom recently where they could have gotten hair from your brush or nail clippings from the wastebasket
  • Anyone who had access to your office or living space
  • People who have offered you food or gifts (many types of curses can be delivered through food, and gifts can be dressed and consecrated to convey curses)

Ask yourself if any of these people would have reason to harm you. Assess whether they would have the ability and knowledge to place a curse themselves and, if not, whether they would pay someone to do it on their behalf. There shouldn't be a lot of candidates who fit the bill. If there are, you have bigger problems than just this one curse.

The Critical Importance of Divination

Whether you can come up with suspects using these methods, or if you just think you know who did it, you should ALWAYS do a divination before attempting a reversal geared at sending a curse back to a specific person. This cannot be stressed enough.

Why divination is essential:

  • If you pick the wrong person, they likely won't feel the effect of the reversal, but they could pick up some bad energy sent their way in the process
  • What you think is a curse might actually be crossed conditions brought on by magickal missteps or inadvertently broken oaths
  • If you attempt to reverse this back upon the sender, you will be sending it back upon yourself
  • Like two mirrors placed face to face, the reflection will go on forever, making the problem worse and worse

Divination Methods:

Write the names of suspects on paper, adding one additional name of "unknown" in case the real culprit is not on your list. Place a pendulum (a lodestone pendulum suspended by your own clipped hair works well, but a store-bought pendulum will work fine) over the first name and ask if that person is the one who placed the curse on you. Clear your mind, connect with the divine, and ask if that name is the name of the one who cursed you. If it is, the pendulum should swing wildly.

Other methods such as drawing cards or runes for each name are equally valid. If you find that you are too scattered to do an effective divination (you are potentially under a hex, after all) or if you are too emotionally invested to get an objective answer, a third party should be brought in to do the divining on your behalf.

Whatever the preferred method, you should rely on divination to confirm your suspicions and to see what outcome will be had. It may be that your reversal will do more harm than good.

A Cautionary Tale

Early in magickal practice, being the target of a nasty jinx can cause minor headaches and broken knick-knacks due to fumbled hands. After searching for curse material, finding a sigil on paper under one of the floor mats in a car can lead to reversing the jinx back upon the sender by burning a candle upside down.

A week or so later, it might come to attention that a girlfriend parted on not-so-good terms with got into a car accident and was in the hospital with serious injuries. She wasn't a serious practitioner, but after confronting her with the sigil, she might admit that she had picked up a book and decided to lay a jinx to show that the target wasn't such a good magickian.

As it happens, most of her jinx would be counteracted by daily rituals and protection measures, measures that she was not taking because she was only a casual practitioner. She received the full force of the jinx she meant to place on the target, and because she had no magickal protection, it was quite destructive.

This is a case where, if the outcome had been known through divination, the jinx would not have been reversed because causing that kind of harm to someone you know, even if they did something against you out of anger, may not align with your ethics or intent.

The lesson: Always divine before reversing. Know what you're sending and where it's going. Understand that an unprepared target will receive the full force of what you send back, and you must be willing to accept responsibility for that outcome.

Solitary & Coven Practice

A coven is a group of witches who practice together, forming a spiritual family committed to the principles of the Craft and to one another. The word originates from the Latin coventus, meaning "assembly" or "agreement" (the same root as covenant). The term first appeared in Scotland around the 1500s.

Solitary vs. Coven Practice

Some witches choose to work alone rather than with a group. A solitary path may suit a witch's temperament, lifestyle, or circumstances, or no coven may be available in their area. Many witches alternate between periods of solitary practice and group work throughout their lives.

Benefits of Solitary Practice

  • Freedom to develop your own style of magickal expression
  • No need to conform to an established group's ideology
  • Flexibility in scheduling and practice

Challenges of Solitary Practice

  • Can feel isolating, especially for beginners
  • Harder to learn without guidance from experienced practitioners
  • Limited to your own energy in spellwork

Guidelines for Solitary Witches

  • Read widely from different authors to gain varied perspectives
  • Meditate regularly to improve mental focus and spiritual connection
  • Make magickal study and practice part of your everyday routine
  • Start with simple rituals and spells, then progress to more complex workings
  • Keep a grimoire of your experiences
  • Learn from mistakes rather than getting discouraged
  • Practice consistently; magick improves with repetition

Benefits of Coven Work

A coven functions as a support group, study center, training program, and spiritual congregation combined. Working with a coven offers:

  • Structured learning about magickal traditions, history, and techniques
  • Group energy that far exceeds what one witch can raise alone
  • Community where you feel accepted and valued
  • Mentorship from more experienced practitioners
  • Shared celebrations of sabbats and meaningful events

The Number Thirteen

Traditional covens have thirteen members, corresponding to the thirteen lunar months in a year. However, many covens include more or fewer members. Smaller groups allow for greater intimacy while reducing the risk of developing unhealthy power dynamics.

Finding a Coven

When searching for a coven, consider these resources:

  • Witchvox (witchvox.com): a longstanding forum for Neopagans with coven listings
  • Local bulletin boards at metaphysical shops, bookstores, health food stores, and yoga centers
  • Online covens and Pagan groups

What to Look For

In Leaders:

  • Skilled facilitation and communication
  • Sensitivity to both individuals and the group as a whole
  • Earned respect through wisdom, responsibility, and consistency
  • Teaching and inspiration without ego or control

In Members:

  • Dedication to the group's goals and traditions
  • Mutual support without gossip or bickering
  • Welcoming attitude that respects newcomers
  • Willingness to share information

Questions to Ask

  • What traditions does the coven follow?
  • What are the attendance and study requirements?
  • What is the initiation process like?
  • Does the group require secrecy? Why?
  • Can you attend an open Circle before considering membership?

Warning Signs

⚠️ Avoid any coven that:
- Requires you to violate your personal ethics or boundaries
- Has members who grovel before leadership
- Charges excessive fees beyond reasonable costs (space rental, supplies)
- Claims to be all-powerful or boasts a 100% success rate

Joining a Coven

If you find a coven that feels right:

  1. Talk with the leader about your interest and what attracted you to the group
  2. Ask about the membership process and when initiations occur
  3. Complete any required study before formal initiation
  4. Consider your role: what skills and talents can you contribute?

Initiation

Initiation rituals vary between covens but typically involve welcoming ceremonies that bond new members to the group. Common elements include:

  • Choosing a magickal name for use in sacred space
  • Greeting each coven member as brothers or sisters in the Craft
  • Symbolic acts like braiding yarn to represent intertwined paths

Some covens have degrees of initiation that members progress through over time.

Many traditions recognize only two degrees: the triangle, and the more advanced pentacle. A coven's male leader is sometimes styled magister or master, and its female leader the high priestess, usually honorary titles reflecting seniority rather than real authority. Some covens mark the triangle grade with a Bracelet and the pentacle grade with a Garter.

If a coven no longer fits your path, you may leave. Try to part on good terms: "Merry meet, merry part, and merry meet again."

Forming Your Own Coven

If no existing coven meets your needs, you might form your own group.

Questions to Consider

  • How many members do you want? (Quality over quantity)
  • What magickal tradition will you follow, if any?
  • Will the group be religious or secular?
  • How will leadership be structured, rotating or defined?
  • Where and when will you meet?
  • What attendance and study requirements will you have?
  • Will you keep a group book of shadows?
  • What festivals will you observe?
  • How will decisions be made?

Building the Group

  1. Approach potential members whose vision aligns with yours
  2. Set a trial period (traditionally a year and a day) before formal membership
  3. Experiment together with various rituals, spells, and meditations
  4. Keep notes on what works and what doesn't
  5. Evaluate at the end: those who wish to continue can formalize; others can part as friends

Living a Magickal Life

Magickal awareness transforms how you experience the world. You begin to:

  • Sense the vibrations of spaces and objects
  • See crystals and herbs as living allies in your work
  • Interpret dreams as messages from your inner self
  • Notice meaningful coincidences and learn from them
  • Feel your connection to all life and the cosmos beyond

Building Your Practice

Start with basics: candles, incense, ribbons, kitchen herbs. Add crystals and gemstones as you progress. Eventually you may acquire traditional tools (wand, chalice, athame, pentagram) or divination tools like tarot cards, a crystal ball, or pendulum. Build your collection as your practice evolves.

Sometimes magick items find you: a friend gifts a tarot deck, a crystal appears on your path. Some witches grow their own herbs, craft their own candles, or create ritual clothing and jewelry.

A Lifelong Path

No matter how long you study, you'll never exhaust the depths of magickal knowledge. Your heritage, temperament, interests, and companions will guide you toward certain traditions and away from others. Despite their different outer forms, most magickal paths share common foundations; learning one tradition often enhances your skill in others.

Magick becomes an integral part of your life and worldview. You may study intensely at times and ease off at others. But once you walk this path, it remains with you.

Choosing a Witch Name

Why Take a Witch Name

A magical name supplements your mundane one and becomes an important part of your emerging witch identity — the name your fellow practitioners will come to know you by.

Method 1: Names of Legend

Many practitioners borrow directly from legendary sorcerers and witches — for example Merlin, Zyto, or Cyprian; or Morgana, Nimue, or Vivienne. Choose one that gives you a genuine thrill and feels appropriately potent and evocative.

Method 2: Mythological & Astrological Names

Look to gods and demigods from any pantheon — Greek, Roman, Norse, Celtic, or otherwise. Your astrological birth sign and ruling planet can point toward a fitting legendary figure whose story resonates with your own nature or craft.

Method 3: Numerology

Convert your everyday name to numbers (A–I = 1–9, J–R = 1–9, S–Z = 1–8), sum the digits, and reduce the total to a single digit. Match that digit to its ruling planet — 1 Sun, 2 Moon, 3 Mars, 4 Mercury, 5 Jupiter, 6 Venus, 7 Saturn, 8 Uranus, 9 Neptune — then look to the myths surrounding that planet for name inspiration.

Method 4: Intuition

If none of the above appeals, let a name arise on its own through reverie or plain instinct. This is ultimately the most important test: the name should feel like a true reflection of who you are beneath the mundane self.

Keeping It Secret

Once chosen, guard your witch name closely — it becomes a key to your deep mind, spoken silently to "switch on" your focus before a working. Share it only with close, trusted practitioners, ideally within a coven, and inscribe it on your tools and jewelry using a witch alphabet such as the Theban Script.

Witches' Working Tools

The Basic Set

Every practicing witch needs a foundational toolkit before ritual work can begin. The four essentials are a white-hilted knife, the Athame, the Chalice, and the Censer.

The Full Complement

Rounding out to eight tools, the complete set is traditionally known by these paired names:

  • The Witches' Knife: also called the Athame or Bolline
  • The Witches' Cord: the Girdle Cord, or cingulum
  • The Witches' Censer: the incense burner, also known as the thurible
  • The Witches' Cup: the chalice
  • The Witches' Spellbook: the Book of Shadows, workbook, or Liber spirituum

From this base toolkit, a witch can go on to craft further magical items: a wand, a speculum, candlesticks, a pentacle, a mandragore or alraun, along with talismans, philters, incenses, images, and amulets.

Exorcism: Purifying Raw Materials

Before any raw material becomes a working tool, it's purified, or exorcised, using salt, water, and incense, which together stand in for the four elements (earth, water, fire, and air). This step symbolically clears the material of outside influence before it's charged with the witch's own will and power, turning a plain object into a magical instrument. This purification process, referred to throughout as exorcism or "passing something through fire and water," comes before the charging step described for individual tools and jewels. See The Charging of Water and Flame for the full formula.

A Witch's Initial Supplies

Beyond the eight core tools, a well-stocked witch also keeps a working supply of everyday materials on hand. Buy these new rather than haggling over price, keep them apart from everyday use, and exorcise each one with fire and water before it's called into a spell:

  • Charcoal blocks for the thurible, self-igniting for preference, though the ordinary kind lit with a few drops of alcohol will do
  • Plain white Candle, six to nine inches long, in beeswax, tallow, or stearin; other colors are called for individually by spell
  • Salt, ground rock salt for preference, though table salt suits most exorcisms
  • Water, tap water for exorcisms and distilled water for philters and elixirs
  • White Masking Tape, handy for temporarily marking out a circle or triangle, especially for group work
  • Plain white Drawing Paper for talismans, or sheepskin parchment if it can be afforded
  • A Geometry Set (compass, protractor, ruler, and set square) for drawing talismans and sigils
  • A small sewing kit: Scissors, Needle, and Thread
  • A Dip Pen, kept as a pen of art, for drawing talismans and writing in the workbook
  • A good quality Paintbrush for painting runes onto magical tools
  • Thick black waterproof Ink, kept as an ink of art, which can be blended with a fitting herb, such as powdered basil for love or cinnamon for intelligence, when a spell calls for it. Tradition-minded witches often brew their own instead of buying it, following a recipe such as Gall Nut Ink or Peach Kernel Ink
  • Household Glue
  • Black and white paint, an enamel that takes well to ceramic, glass, and metal, used as a paint of art for inscribing runes on working tools
  • A small table set aside for practice, sometimes called the table of practice or altar
  • An assortment of jars and Bottle for philters and powders
  • Adhesive Labels to keep every preparation clearly identified
  • A sharp, white-hilted knife for preparatory cutting and engraving, the Bolline

These form only a starting stock. Build it up gradually as spells call for special herbs or extra supplies, and keep everything magical together, ideally in a dedicated cupboard, closet, or room.

Ritual Gestures

Gestures are physical expressions of intent used in Sabbat rituals, invocations, and energy work. Each position of the body communicates something specific to the forces being called upon.

Indicating the Goddess

Hold the palms up with arms open and raised. This posture receives and honors the feminine Divine.

Indicating the God

Cross the arms against the chest with palms turned inward. This gesture is used during Solar phases of passage: Lughnassadh, Mabon, and Samhain.

Expressing Unity

Begin with palms facing outward, gathering energy from the air. Turn the hands with palms inward and draw them to the chest, blending external and internal energies at the heart. Then thrust the hands back outward in front of the body with the heel of the palms down, fingertips up, pushing outward to return excess energy.

Use this gesture once for unity, twice for balance, and three times for completion. It may be used when calling the Quarters as well as during invocation of the Lady and the Lord.

Drawing Divine Blessings

Place the palms inward against the chest, then extend the arms with hands motioned away, palms down. Move the hands outward to release excessive energies. This gesture draws Divine blessings and energy inward before returning the surplus.

Accessing Universal Energy

Raise the arms and hands into a teepee position overhead, with the heel of the palms nearly touching, the center of the palms angled back, and the fingers bent inward like a blossom or bowl. Bring the hands down on either side of the head, palms up, until level with the shoulders. This draws Divine energy into balance with the personal energy of the third eye and crown, augmenting receptivity.

Hold this position through the invocation. Then move to the hands against the chest and motion outward to complete the cycle.

Tea Leaf Reading

A method of reading symbols formed by tea leaves in a cup to answer questions and glimpse future events.

Choosing Your Tea

Before beginning a reading, choose your tea with intention. Each variety carries its own energetic signature and will shape the quality of the information that comes through.

Black Tea

Black tea aligns with the energy of the crone, the waning moon, and the threshold between the living and the dead. It is the tea of choice when seeking wisdom from ancestors, messages from those who have passed, or when working within a New Moon ritual context. The fermentation process strips away the softness of the fresh leaf, transforming it through solar energy and time into something more potent. Witches understand death not as an ending but as a passage, and black tea carries that knowledge in its cup.

Green Tea

Green tea carries the energy of optimism, growth, and renewal. Use it when your question involves change: a decision to be made, a move being considered, a pattern ready to be released and replaced. Its fresh-leaf origin aligns it with emerging possibilities rather than established conditions.

Moroccan Tea

Moroccan tea is brewed as a green tea infusion poured over freshly chopped mint. The addition of mint brings its prosperity and fortune associations into the reading, making this blend ideal for questions about money, career, and financial direction.

First and Second Flush

Flush refers to the harvest timing of the tea leaves, not the variety. First flush teas are gathered from the earliest spring growth, connecting them to maiden energy and new beginnings. Use first flush green tea when seeking insight on romantic possibilities and the opening of love. Second flush teas are harvested in the fullness of summer and carry a more mature, settled energy. Use second flush when reading on established relationships, long-term commitments, or family dynamics.

Oolong

Oolong sits between green and black tea, only partially fermented. This in-between nature makes it especially suited to readings about crossroads and mixed conditions. When you are weighing two clear options, navigating ambiguity, or finding that cards like the Chariot or the Tower keep appearing in your spreads without resolution, oolong is the tea to brew.

How to Read Tea Leaves

When preparing tea for a reading, do not strain the leaves. Leave them loose in the cup.

The Process

  1. Focus clearly on your question while drinking the tea.
  2. Drink all but a small amount of liquid, leaving the leaves behind.
  3. Swirl the remaining liquid and leaves gently around the cup.
  4. Turn the cup upside down onto the saucer, positioning the handle at the six o'clock position.
  5. Rotate the overturned cup three times on the saucer.
  6. Return the cup to its upright position.

Reading the Symbols

Read the symbols that appear in the cup by moving clockwise from the handle. Events expected soonest will appear closest to the handle, with timing extending further around the cup as you go.

See the Symbol Grimoire for interpretation of common shapes and figures.

Symbol Types

Tasseomancy is highly intuitive and relies on a strong command of symbolic association. The shapes that appear in the leaves fall into five general categories:

  • Numbers
  • Letters
  • Specific objects
  • Identifiable animals
  • Mythical creatures or beings

Cup Positions

Where a symbol appears is as significant as the symbol itself. Read from the handle clockwise:

  • The rim: The present moment, the questioner's current frame of reality.
  • The sides: The near future, the sphere of influence just about to come to pass.
  • The bottom: The distant future, an outcome that will take time to materialize and will be shaped by the actions the questioner takes or does not take.
  • The handle: The questioner's immediate environment, the circumstances under which they are currently living and working.

The Reading

The diviner prepares the tea and the questioner drinks in a meditative state, allowing a clear question to form inwardly. The questioner need not share the question; a skilled reader works through the herbs' connection to source energy and truth surfaces regardless. Sharing the question, however, allows the diviner to contextualize symbols more precisely and interpret both their type and placement together.

Customizing Your Blend

Tasseomancy draws on all four classical elements: the herbs carry earth and air, the water comes from the kettle, and fire heats it. You can deepen this elemental alignment by choosing herbs that correspond to your specific question. Use loose-leaf tea that is chopped but not heavily processed so the leaves form readable shapes in the cup.

A few starting points:

  • Rosemary for questions touching on past memories or ancestral themes
  • Rose to amplify readings focused on love and relationships
  • Mint for questions about luck, fortune, and financial direction

For a wider correspondence reference, see the individual tea pages and the Tea Magick Guide.

Coffee Grounds Reading

Reading coffee grounds (tasseography) is a companion practice originating in Turkey and extending across the Middle East, where it has been practiced since the 1600s. Turkish coffee's thick, sediment-rich preparation makes it a particularly readable medium.

Preparing the Coffee

The coffee must be ground to a very fine powder; the degree of grind matters more than the quality of the bean. Combine the ground coffee and sugar (if desired) in a small copper Turkish coffee pot, fill with water, and bring to a medium boil. When foam accumulates at the top (within about 5 minutes), spoon the foam into a white cup, boil the grounds a few seconds longer, then pour everything over the foam.

The Reading Process

The questioner drinks the coffee, then places a saucer over the rim. They swirl the cup three times, invert it onto the saucer, and allow it to rest for about 10 minutes. The diviner then reads the symbols in the grounds, using the same intuitive and symbolic approach as tea leaf reading.

Cup Positions

The coffee cup is read along two axes:

PositionEnergy
NorthNegative influence
SouthPositive influence
EastNear future
WestDistant future

Both the cup and the saucer are read: the cup reflects the questioner's outer life (work, commerce, livelihood), while the saucer reflects their inner and home life (relationships, matters of the heart). Note the size, intensity, and distribution of symbols as well as any significant trails or shapes in the sediment.

Elements in Spell-casting

The Western magickal tradition recognizes four foundational forces that shape reality and fuel spellwork: Air, Earth, Fire, and Water. Each carries its own living, distinct energy, and understanding how they operate, both individually and in combination, is key to building effective rituals.

The Four Pillars

Air and Fire are traditionally classified as masculine or yang forces, while Earth and Water carry feminine or yin qualities. Life takes root in earth and water, but it needs air and fire to ignite the process. Strong magickal practice grows from keeping these forces in healthy equilibrium.

Every element holds power that is singular, purposeful, and alive in its own right. Depending on the goal of your working, you may call on one element more heavily than the others. But real potency often comes from the interplay between them. When elements converge and form a threshold, something new emerges. Steam, for instance, is born from the meeting of water and fire, and it carries potent energy for spiritual cleansing and shielding.

Elemental Influence on the Practitioner

These forces shape people as much as they shape spells. At least one element will hold sway in any given birth chart, shaping temperament and determining which forms of magick come most naturally. The zodiac affiliations below offer a starting point, but a full birth chart gives the real picture. Someone born under Taurus (an earth sign) who has five planets in water signs, for example, will resonate far more with water than their sun sign alone suggests.

Air

Air acts as a carrier and a messenger. In magickal thinking (and in certain branches of advanced physics), nothing that exists ever truly vanishes, the phrase "disappearing into thin air" is meant quite literally in spell-casting. When a candle burns, it draws on fire's power but also summons air: whatever the flame consumes passes into the atmosphere. Air is tied to astral travel as well; the image of witches soaring through the sky reflects voyages taken in dreamwork and visionary states.

Air is a masculine, yang force. Fragrance speaks its language, and word-based charms tap directly into its power.

Zodiac signs: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius

Earth

Earth functions as both power source and foundation, fueling growth while keeping everything solid and grounded. For anyone venturing into magickal realms, earth supplies the force that keeps you rooted and present. Practitioners benefit from spending time in the garden (even without gardening), going barefoot when possible, working with real clay, or simply playing in the mud. A spa mud bath counts, too.

Earth is a feminine, yin force. Its magickal power flows through plants drawn from the ground, clay figures molded by hand, and raw soil, cemetery dust, crossroads earth, and similar materials.

Zodiac signs: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn

Fire

Fire is the most self-willed of the elements, answering to no one and resisting every attempt at containment. It can heal, charge, scrub clean, and refine. It is the great transformer, and it demands respect above all else. While any element can turn dangerous (floods, mudslides, tornadoes), fire is typically the most hazardous. No amount of spiritual focus replaces common-sense fire safety. Never assume that ritual context makes open flame risk-free. Stay alert.

Fire is a masculine, yang force. Candle magick is its most popular expression, but magickal bonfires and oil lamps serve the same purpose. Magick mirrors sometimes harness the raw, shape-shifting force of flame, creative and destructive in equal measure.

Zodiac signs: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius

Water

Water is the element most closely linked to magick itself. It is the origin point of life, not only in the Darwinian sense but in the most intimate way imaginable: every one of us begins life floating in amniotic fluid. It governs psychic perception and deep intuitive awareness.

Water is a feminine, yin force. Spells rooted in water take shape in the bath, along the shoreline, or beside any natural body of water. They make use of moon-blessed water, ritually prepared washes, and collected rain.

Zodiac signs: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces

How the Elements Pair and Combine

Fire and Water sit at opposite poles, extreme yang and extreme yin, forming one matched pair, while Earth and Air balance each other. But like all yin/yang forces, the elements do not exist in isolation. A spell can run on a single element (an Air-powered word charm, for example), yet most workings blend two or more.

Incense is a clear illustration: botanical matter (Earth) meets flame (Fire) to produce fragrant smoke (Air). A more layered spell, dressing a candle with botanical oil, then burning it while bathing in a magickal infusion, engages all four elements at once.

Beyond the Western Four

The four-element model of Air, Earth, Fire, and Water is the standard Western framework and the one most magickal traditions share. It is not, however, the only system:

  • Chinese magick traditionally counts five elements. Metal plays a significant role across many traditions, but Chinese philosophy elevates it to full elemental status alongside the Western four.
  • Jewish magick traditionally counts three elements. Air (or ether) is considered so pervasive and omnipresent that it does not need to be named separately, leaving Water, Earth, and Fire as the recognized trio.

Elements as the First Symbols

It takes little imagination to suppose that the very first symbols our ancestors noticed, and tried to make sense of, were the natural features around them. Long before anyone thought to score marks into sand or scratch them onto rock, people looked to the landscape and the elements to find their place in the universe. Open a door and see what is there, a mountain or a tower block, trees or walls, a river or a stretch of water. Whatever it is, we turn these features into symbols, representative images of our realm of experience, and they become as much a part of our inner landscape as our outer one. The great leap comes when we realize that our private reading of reality, in whatever form it takes, belongs to a collective consciousness.

The most easily shared experience of natural symbols comes when we look to the skies, the common ground of all humanity, visible to everyone and full of regular features that let us measure time. Little wonder that the Sun, with its reliable rising and setting and its glorious power to illuminate, became the ultimate symbol of the Godhead in whatever form that takes.

We like to lay our own ideas over the natural world, defining our place within it by ordering it somehow, finding or inventing patterns and making order out of chaos. The Gaia hypothesis, named for the Greek goddess of the Earth and proposed by James Lovelock, holds that every living thing shapes its environment to keep it fit for life, and that humankind, for all its limited perspective, is an inherent part of that platform. It is no coincidence that Lovelock's vision of complete cohesion arrived alongside the first photograph of the Earth, taken by an unmanned spacecraft in late 1967. As Stewart Brand said at the time, it was so graphic, this little blue, white, green, and brown jewel of an icon set against a featureless black vacuum, and this is all we have, so we have to make it work.

The Four Aspects of Being

The elements carry a visceral significance, answering to our emotions and states of being and shaping the character of a whole range of things. Among these are the four humors of the natural world, hot, cold, moist, and dry, along with the signs of the zodiac and the colors. For alchemists they also map onto the four aspects of the human being: fire is the spirit, water the soul, air the mind, and earth the body. Here again the microcosm and the macrocosm fold into one another, and the Platonic solids gather the full range of elements within their geometric forms.

The Fifth Element

In the West the fifth element, aether or ether, is often overlooked. Aether is the essential unifying principle, a reminder that the universe is built from a unified diversity. It is the quintessence that holds the other four in relation, the still center from which the rest take their meaning.

Balance, Heaven, and Hell

Heaven, in symbolic terms, is the correct balance of all the elements working in harmony, and Hell is the corresponding imbalance. Popularly Hell is imagined as a place of excess fire, yet it is just as well symbolized by the savage winds that scour a desert, carrying with them the pestilential demons of the Assyrian pantheon, such as Pazuzu and Lilitu. Tellingly, when the elements fall out of balance on the Earth, we call the result a natural disaster.

Sacred Geometry of the Elements

The simple geometric shapes that serve as a code for the elements form a fundamental part of reading symbols. These shapes combine and juxtapose to make profound statements and to inspire ideas that strive toward harmony between opposing forces. Squaring the circle is one such device, a way of joining spirit with matter and the created universe with the greater cosmos, and it sits at the root of both sacred and secular geometry. In the same spirit, the upward-pointing triangle of fire meets the downward-pointing triangle to form the six-pointed star, a sign that unites earth with the heavens. All of this echoes the alchemical principle "as above, so below," repeated across the world and folded into the Lord's Prayer in the words "thy will be done, on Earth as it is in Heaven."

Death Spells: Death, Ghosts, Necromancy & Vampires

Death magick is not about causing death, and there are no killing curses here. As a category, death spells concern the topic of death itself, its aftermath, its spiritual mechanics, and its effects on both the departed and those left behind. Though practitioners may be buried with their tools, the overwhelming majority of death spells are crafted for the living.

This is a spell category that walks the edge between religion, spirituality, and magick. Work these spells, or adapt them, according to your own spiritual framework.

What Death Spells Actually Do

Death spells typically fall into three categories:

  • Preparing and propitiating the dead so they move peacefully into the next existence. Correct funerary rites are essential. Incorrect or absent rites may produce ghosts, demons, vampires, or general spiritual unrest.
  • Protecting the living from the dead: shielding against lingering presences, hostile energies, or souls that could not properly cross over.
  • Accessing the dead's special powers: including necromancy, petitioning ancestor spirits, or working with the dead's accumulated wisdom, with or without their cooperation.

Death Magick & Modern Culture

Many of these workings are ancient and assume that the dead are prepared at home, by someone who either knew the deceased or was trained in proper magickal procedure. This stands in stark contrast to contemporary industrialized society, where death is outsourced to professionals and kept carefully out of sight.

Magickal traditions hold the preparation of the body and funerary rites to be critically important. The consequences of getting it wrong affect both the living and the dead:

  • Without correct funerary ritual, a soul becomes vulnerable, susceptible to capture by a sorcerer, who may put it to work as a magickal instrument or servitor. This belief is documented at least as far back as ancient Babylon and echoes in traditions like the duppies of the West Indies.
  • A spirit unable to transition properly has nowhere to go, and may take out that frustration on the living. This is especially true of those who died through violence or were never identified.
  • In many traditions, death leads to ancestorhood: the honored dead serve and protect their descendants. Without proper rites and ongoing offerings, that protective relationship cannot form, leaving the living undefended and the dead resentful.

Historical Context: Preparing to Die

This was not always solely a concern for the living. Ancient Egyptian and Tibetan traditions required that certain spells and rituals be learned in life so that they could be performed after death. The soul navigating its afterlife examinations the way a student prepares for a difficult entrance exam.

The Tibetan Book of the Dead (The Book of the Great Liberation) and the Egyptian Book of the Dead (The Book of Going Forth by Day) document these traditions. Over time in Egypt, the practice shifted: the wealthy were simply buried with Books of the Dead as amulets, essentially glorified hall passes for the afterlife.

📝
A note on organization: Spells to prevent the formation of ghosts and vampires, particularly those centered on funerary rites and immediate post-death rituals, belong with Death Spells. Spells dealing with already-formed, "mature" ghosts and vampires fall under their own categories.

Death Spirits

Death Spirits, spirits of death, carry an innate unease that is not simply modern squeamishness. Our ancestors felt it too. These spirits serve necessary functions, and that necessity makes them powerful allies when approached correctly, at the right moment, for the right purpose.

Death Spirits tend to fall into two types:

  1. Transition spirits: those involved in the dying process itself, easing the soul from one state to the next.
  2. Guardians: those who preside over the realms of the dead, rule cemeteries and cremation grounds, and keep the dead where they belong.

Many guardian spirits of death's threshold go unnamed deliberately. As with spirits of disease, there is a long tradition of avoiding their true names lest they be summoned unintentionally. Epithets and euphemisms serve instead. Hades literally means "the unseen one." When even that grew too familiar, he was called Polydegmon ("the hospitable one," because all are eventually welcome in his realm) or Pluton ("wealth," since ultimately he possesses everyone and everything).

Guardians of the Dead & the Cemetery Gates

  • Baron Samedi and La Grande Brigitte: leaders of the Vodoun Ghede spirits
  • Dongyue Dadi, Lord of Tai Shan (China)
  • Erishkigal / Lamashtu (Mesopotamia)
  • Hades and Persephone (Greece)
  • Hel (Norse)
  • Kali, Shiva, Yama (Hindu)
  • Mictlantecuhtli and Mictecacíhuatl: the Aztec Lord and Lady of the Dead
  • Oya (Yoruba)
  • Osiris (Egypt)
  • Yambe-Akka (Saami)

These guardians may be petitioned to protect the souls of the dead, to maintain order among the departed, and, when appropriate, to grant access to the spirits of the dead.

Psychopomps

Psychopomp comes from the Greek for "conductor of souls." These spirits specialize in guiding souls between the land of the living and the land of the dead. They also serve as sponsors and protectors for shamans who travel between realms.

You may recognize a psychopomp in dreams or visions by the objects they carry: a key (threshold crossing), a cutting instrument (severing ties with the living), and/or a torch (illuminating the path ahead). The Etruscan psychopomp Culso, for instance, arrives at death holding scissors in one hand, to sever the soul's connection to the living world, and a blazing torch in the other, to light the way into whatever comes next.

Psychopomps Across Traditions

  • Gabriel, Azrael, and the unnamed Angel of Death (Jewish)
  • Anubis, Hathor, Wepwawet (Egypt)
  • Baron Samedi, Baron La Croix, Baron Cimetière (Vodoun)
  • Culso (Etruscan)
  • The Valkyries and Freya (Norse)
  • Giltinė (Lithuanian)
  • Hekate and Hermes (Greece)
  • Jizō (Japan)
  • Mother Holle (German)

Animal Psychopomps

Animals serve as psychopomps as well. Dogs, jackals, and canines are the most widely attested, including Anubis (jackal), Kali (jackal), Hekate (dog), and Wepwawet (wolf). Other animal psychopomps include butterflies, snakes, and birds, particularly ravens, crows, hornbills, and frigatebirds.

If any of these animals appear spontaneously at a funeral or death rite, it is considered deeply auspicious: the soul's escort has arrived. Their presence is meant to comfort and reassure the living that the crossing is underway.

Psychopomps may be petitioned by either the dying person or by their loved ones, to ease the passage and ensure a safe transition.

People in Spell-casting

Every spell begins with a person. Without a practitioner's intent and direction, magickal energy simply radiates outward without focus or purpose. Yet some workings draw on more than the energy, desire, and creative force of a single individual.

Working with Partners

Not every spell is performed alone. Healing and cleansing rites, in particular, often need to be carried out on behalf of the person who stands to benefit. Choosing spell partners wisely is essential. Each participant's personal energy flows through the working just as powerfully as any botanical, mineral, or elemental force. It is equally important to exclude anyone whose presence might weaken the outcome, whether through deliberate interference or simple misalignment of intention. Select collaborators whose goals mirror your own and who genuinely want to see your work succeed.

The Power of the Body

A complete, living person is not always necessary for a working. Different parts of the human body are understood to carry their own distinct magickal charge, and just as each serves a unique biological function, each performs a different role in spellwork. In most cases, the body part's power is represented symbolically through an image rather than through the part itself. This is the principle behind the milagro, a small metal charm shaped like a specific piece of anatomy. Eyes, genitals, hands, and hearts are the most frequently depicted, and they appear most often in healing and protective workings.

Personal Concerns

Occasionally a spell calls for something more tangible than a symbolic image. "Part" is not quite the right word, since no pain is involved in obtaining these materials. The body naturally sheds certain substances that retain the essence of the person they came from and maintain an energetic link back to that individual. Manipulating these shed materials gives a practitioner a direct channel to the person who produced them. In Hoodoo tradition, they go by the name personal concerns.

Because personal concerns expose the source individual to magickal influence, they could, in theory, serve hostile aims. In reality, though, harmful use represents only a fraction of how they are actually put to work.

Casting Spells Using Names

Most magickal systems view a person's name as part of their intrinsic identity, a source of great power and vulnerability. Just as the subtle body (aura) extends beyond the physical form, a name carries an energetic signature that can be targeted in spellwork.

True Names

Knowing someone's true name grants power over them. Historically, people were given multiple names: one for public use, one for ritual use, and a secret name known only to the individual. Mothers would whisper a hidden name into their baby's ear, never to be repeated, ensuring one name always remained protected. In ancient Egypt, possessing such exceptional magick power that even one's own mother didn't know one's true name was the highest praise.

The Mother's Name

The connection between name and mother holds deep magickal significance. While patriarchal cultures identified people through the father's name, magick spells and magickal documents have always used the mother's name instead. The reasoning is practical: a mother's identity is never in question, making the mother's name the only reliable way to guarantee correct identification in a working.

The standard magickal formula for writing or calling someone's name is: "[Name], child of [their mother's name]."

Names of Power

Angels, demons, and spirits of all kinds are summoned by calling their true name. They supposedly cannot resist the call, and much summoning magick depends upon this premise.

Correct pronunciation is essential. This knowledge was originally transmitted orally, and significant disagreement exists among historians, magickal practitioners, and scholars over how even well-known Greek and Egyptian deity names should be pronounced.

Some spell-casting traditions incorporate long series of magickal names. The Magickal Papyri contain examples of these spells, though the names lack surviving mythological context and may not have been recognized even by practitioners of that era.

When working with Names of Power, exercise caution and discernment. Rather than reciting unfamiliar names, consider using Names of Power you have a personal connection with: trusted Spirits, ancestral spirits, or living people whose assistance you value and trust.
