Rune Grimoire

Runic Cosmology

The rune mysteries unfold within a vast cosmological framework. Grasping this structure is essential groundwork before approaching the theories and practice of rune magick.

The Rune World

Prior to the birth of time, only Ginnungagap existed: a "magickally charged void." At its southern edge a realm of fire blazed into being, Muspellsheimr, while at its northern boundary Niflheimr condensed as the "mist world." Waves of frozen rime poured from Niflheimr and filled the northern reaches of the gap, even as Muspellsheimr hurled sparks and glowing matter outward. Between these two extremes, the center held still, "mild as windless air."

Where fire and ice collided, the frozen substance melted and the latent yeast quickened under Muspellsheimr's power. From this reaction the primal giant Ymir took shape, whose name ("the roarer") points to the concept of primal vibration. Ymir was androgynous, and from this being the rime-giant races descended.

The cosmic cow Audhumla materialized from the dripping rime and nourished Ymir with her milk. By licking the salty ice blocks she uncovered the archetypal being Buri, likewise androgynous. Buri's line produced Borr, who took Bestla (daughter of a rime-giant) as his wife. Their three sons were Odin, Vili, and Ve, embodying inspiration, will, and holiness. Together they slew Ymir and shaped the world from the substance of his cosmic body. From this refashioned world they then created the first man and woman, Askr and Embla ("ash" and "elm"), endowing them with a range of spiritual gifts.

Key Principles of the Runic Cosmogony

  • There is no personal Creator: cosmogony is seen as a natural and organic process
  • The universe ultimately derives from a single source, Ginnungagap, which divides itself into two extremes of fire (expansive energy) and ice (primal matter/antimatter)
  • This polarity is mutually attracted, and from their reunion the primal essence and archetypal pattern for manifestation are formed
  • From this framework the multiplicity of being evolves

The Nine Worlds

Once creation had been stabilized, the multiverse consisted of Nine Worlds, contained in and supported by the World-Tree, Yggdrasill. These worlds contain countless abodes and dwellings. In the center is Midhgardhr, with the other worlds arrayed around, above, and below it:

  • North: Niflheimr (mist world)
  • East: Jotunheimr (Etin-world)
  • South: Muspellsheimr (fire world)
  • West: Vanaheimr (Vanir-world)
  • Above Midhgardhr: Ljossalfheimr (light-elf-world)
  • Above Ljossalfheimr: Asgardhr (enclosure of the Aesir, which houses many dwellings)
  • Below Midhgardhr: Svartalfheimr (black-elf-world, or dwarf-world)
  • Below Svartalfheimr: Hel (the silent, still, and sleepy realm of the dead)

Between and among these worlds the runes and their roadways are to be found.

Manifestation of the Rune Row

The manifestation of the runes and their ordering in the Futhark row are bound up with the cosmogonic and cosmological processes. The runes have no point of origin; they are the substance of the latent energy contained in Ginnungagap. The runes exist simultaneously in an undifferentiated state throughout the void, and thus defy comprehension.

Shining Runes and Dark Runes

At the division between Muspellsheimr and Niflheimr, the runic forces are polarized into shining runes (Old Norse heidhrúnar) and dark runes (Old Norse myrkrúnar). These are polarized aspects of the entire corpus of runic power expressed simultaneously. These runic forces attract one another, in order that they might rejoin and create the cosmic seed of manifestation contained in Ymir.

The shining runes and dark runes are reassimilated in a pattern capable of manifestation. The runic forces are at work throughout the cosmogonic processes; however, the runes as we know them have not been manifested, because the entire process, up to the sacrifice of Ymir, takes place in an unmanifested state.

The Sacrifice of Ymir and the Ordering

When Odin, Vili, and Ve sacrifice Ymir (the crystallized seed form of the collective runic pattern), they arrange this runic "substance" in accordance with the multiversal pattern. Thus they "create" the Nine Worlds and Yggdrasill. This primal act brings about cosmic order and manifestation.

At this point the runes are ordered in the Futhark row in their linear form as the primary arrangement at the center of the multiverse. This manifestation unfolds from the "inside out," beginning with the most basic forms of cyclical and vertical force.

The Twelve-Fold Spherical Law

From that point the other runes manifest themselves in a linear pattern governed by a twelve-fold spherical law. As each succeeding circle is manifested, a pair of runes (esoteric concepts) are isolated within the "space." The laws of sympathy and antipathy determine which runes crystallize in each circle. Those same laws govern which of these two concepts will be aligned with which previously manifested rune in the row.

The row thus produced is perceived by the intellect in an order governed by the path of the sun, and thereby the runes manifest their numerical values 1 through 24. These numerical values are also part of the innate relative positions of one mystery to the others, and play a determining role in their ordering.

The Ættir and the Eightfold Star

The ættir are ruled by the pattern of the eightfold "cross" or "star" by which the ancient Northmen divided the heavens. These patterns, as well as those that govern the linear alignment of the staves, are fruitful avenues of meditation and will reveal much wisdom and provide great power to the vitki who can unravel their riddles.

Elements

Throughout the runic cosmology there are forces that might be called "elements," such as fire, water, ice, air, and earth. These are reminiscent of the Platonic-Hermetic elements but are not to be understood as identical with them. Both systems have common roots in the Indo-European spring of wisdom, which recognizes observation of nature (both internal and external) as the most reliable clue to the nature of numinous reality. The proximity of the Northern peoples to the realms of ice led them to recognize the multiversal dichotomy between fire and ice.

ElementAttributes
FireTotal expansion, heat, all-vibration, archetypal energy
AirAll-pervasiveness and omnipresence, formless space, motion, light, intellect, communication
WaterArchetypal unmanifested form, evolutionary being, stillness, darkness, unconscious
IceTotal contraction, coldness (distinct from Isa), no-vibration, cohesiveness
EarthTotal potential (containing all the others), archetypal manifestation and framework, physical matter, existence

An intuitive feel for these ideas will serve the vitki well in understanding cosmological mysteries, as well as providing emotional links to the various runes.

Streams of Runic Force

These streams of runic force may be classified according to the realms in which they originate:

  1. Terrestrial streams run along the surface of the earth
  2. Heavenly streams circulate in the atmosphere
  3. Chthonic streams flow in the subterranean sphere

These streams or fields constantly interact upon one another, causing changes and fluctuations in the intensity and form of the force found in each realm. All runes exist in all realms; they are, however, concentrated and intensified in power within the realms most sympathetic to the force they embody.

Through the practices of stadhagaldr and meditation the vitki is able to draw these cosmic streams into their own personal runic sphere, there to be integrated (for increased personal power) or re-projected in order to cause changes in accordance with the will of the vitki.

The word "stream" is perhaps a bit misleading. Actually, these runic forces may be felt as a variety of sensations within the psyche. Some are indeed similar to flowing streams of power; others are akin to waves, or whirlpools, or utter stillness. Each vitki should explore the feel of each rune on its own terms. Once contact has been made, it will be unmistakable.

The Soul and Personal Power

Understanding the old Nordic soul-construct and personal power conceptions is essential, for these play a prominent role in the theories of rune magick.

The Divine Gifts

Certain soul qualities were given to the primal man and woman (coequally and simultaneously) by the triad of gods: Odhinn, Vili, and Ve. In the Voluspa:

Until the Aesir,
mighty and loving,
came from the host
to the coast;
on the land they found
of little might
Askr and Embla
yet unfated.
They had not ond,
they had not odhr,
neither la nor laeti
nor good litr;
Odhinn gave ond,
Hoenir gave odhr,
Lodhurr gave la
and good litr.

The last three gifts indicate external qualities (la: appearance; laeti: movement; litr: health). The two central gifts are:

  • Ond is the breath of life, the "spirit" that is the divine spark in mankind and the all-pervasive force that penetrates and animates the multiverse. Akin to the Indian conception of prana (breath) and etymologically connected to Sanskrit atman (soul).
  • Odhr is the power of inspiration and ecstasy. The name Odhinn is derived from the same root word. This is the pure and irrational numinous power that is the magickal faculty of gods and men.

Nornic Force and Divine Structure

With the entrance of the Nornic force, time and the laws of cause and effect arise (see Pertho). The infusion of divine structure and consciousness provided by Heimdallr/Odin (see Mannaz) provides another numinous force, handed down through the generations and increased or decreased according to human action.

The Four Soul Entities

  1. Hugr is the conscious will and intellect
  2. Hamr is the personal aspect of the plastic image-forming essence in the cosmos, bridging spiritual and physical worlds. A powerful hugr can project this essence to another location in an almost physical manner
  3. Hamingja means "shape-changing force," "luck," "power." It may be transferred from one person to another, from a person to an object, or projected into space. This force may be increased continuously by ritualized magickal action and deeds of honor
  4. Fylgja (fetch) is the storehouse of action, symbolized by a female figure, an animal, or a crescent shape. Fylgja imparts the orlog (fate) of the person in accordance with past action

Both hamingja and fylgja may be passed from one generation to the next as a type of "reincarnation."

Dynamistic and Animistic Forces

The forces at work in magick fall broadly into two categories. Dynamistic powers are largely mechanistic, operating without significant consciousness. The runes themselves belong in this category. Animistic forces include all the various wights, gods (Aesir and Vanir), elves, dwarves, and giants. The gods are archetypes: exemplary models of consciousness perceived as animate primordial images.

These archetypal models also serve as powerful tools in magick, functioning either as internal consciousness factors or as symbols and vehicles for consciously directed power in invocatory rites.

Communication as the Core Pattern

Regardless of the type of power a magician works with, the fundamental pattern of action is communication. The runes form a channel of connection between the will of the vitki and the universe.

Personal Runes and World Runes

Rune streams permeate the multiverse and have corresponding structures within the personal sphere, seated in the hamingja. The "personal runes" and "world runes" are consciously synthesized in the magickal act. This synthesis is the essence of the Old Norse concepts heill (holy, wholeness) and heill hugr (whole mind).

The rune staves act as keys, granting access to these streams both within the self and in the causal multiversal realms. Through willed ritual action, the vitki manipulates the runic forces across the Nine Worlds. Through the laws of Pertho, these actions become manifest.

The God-Forms

The god-forms housed in the rune realms are holy archetypes and consciousness modalities that preexisted human self-consciousness but are intensified by human action. Each type of wight inhabits a world suited to its kind, though no well-defined borders separate most of these realms.

The Tripartite Divine Society

The runic god-forms can be understood through a threefold matrix plus a fourth category (see Mannaz):

  1. Sovereignty (dual: judicial and magickal kingship)
  2. Strength (the warrior function)
  3. Production (dual: the divine twins and the holy brother and sister)

The major deities align accordingly:

  1. The Judge-King (Tiwaz/Tyr) or the Priest-Magician (Odin)
  2. The Warrior (Thor, in his oldest aspect)
  3. The Providers (Freyja and Freyr, or Alcis)

Odin has aspects in all three levels. Freyja likewise spans all three: goddess of fertility, teacher of seidhr magick to Odin, and half of all warriors slain in battle go to her in Folkvangr.

The fourth category encompasses "deified" dynamistic forces: the sun (Sunna/Sol), the moon (Mani), and fire (embodied in Kenaz, Nauthiz, and Dagaz).

Applying the Divine Paradigm in Ritual

  • Third function (Freyja, Freyr): powerful aids in rites of fertility, art, craft, wealth, and eroticism
  • Second function (Thor): rules in operations of protection, defense, liberation, and curses
  • First function, Tyr aspect: most valuable in rites of law, order, justice, and victory
  • First function, Odin aspect: the most comprehensive, especially powerful in rites to obtain wisdom, numinous knowledge, personal power, and to bind or constrict enemies

Like Odin, the vitki should search restlessly across all worlds, seeking wisdom and power, always willing to sacrifice self to self, and constantly sharing that wisdom with others of like mind.

Methods of Rune Magick

Runes may be magickally employed in a wide variety of ways, all of which remain valid and potent for modern practice.

Talismanic Magick

The most common method of rune magick in ancient times was talismanic: runes were inscribed into objects and infused with psychic power to effect change in the vitki or their environment. Hundreds of runic talismans have survived, and studying them reveals deep insight into the magickal techniques used to create them.

One dramatic example comes from the Egilssaga (chapter 44): the hero Egill suspects poison in a drink offered to him, so he stabs his palm, carves runes on the drinking horn, and colors the runic forms with his blood. The horn shatters and the poison flows away.

The Tine as a Living Being

A rune tine is not merely an inscribed object. It is a living being with an ørlög bestowed upon it by the vitki. The runester gives the object life and then provides it with ørlög through the nature of the runic power used to load it. The living nature of the tine may become so strongly enforced that it develops a discernible personality. To facilitate this state of autonomous, vitki-willed force, the runester may choose to give the tine a name during the loading ritual. This is the mystery behind the many runic talismans, especially weapons, that bear personal names.

Loading and Unloading

The technical theories behind tine magick align perfectly with the laws of action within the runic cosmology. The rune tine acts as a key to unlock the power of particular rune streams. During the loading process, these streams (identical with hamingja) are willfully blended in the causal worlds and infused into the object, which has been prepared by the vitki with signs and staves receptive to those forces. There the streams are intensified or modified and released again, bearing a specific character imparted by the ørlög-giving galdrar and formalár of the vitki and the innate power of the symbols depicted on the tine. The talismanic form becomes linked to the essence of the particular rune or runes through a great concentration and energizing of forces directed by the vitki into the tine, using the shape, sound, and color of the runes.

Once the tine has been properly loaded, this power is then unloaded according to the form the vitki impressed upon it. The object becomes the center of a vortex of force, receiving energy, formulating it in accordance with its ørlög, and re-expressing it in the causal realms to produce the desired result. This power may also be retained within the personal sphere. The efficiency of the process depends on the level of strength in the vitki's hamingja and the quality of concentration and visualization brought to bear during the loading operation.

Death of Rune Tines

In most runic formalar, not only should the definite purpose of the talismanic being be stated but also the length of time the wight is to live, that is, be vivified with magickal force. A convenient formula for this duration is "until thy work is wrought."

Since the wight of the tine is a living being, its death should be attended with proper ritual. This ensures that the magickal force stored in the form is redirected back to its source (the vitki), or offered as a form of sacrifice.

There are two principal methods for effecting this important ritual act:

1. Funeral Rites of Reabsorption

This method emphasizes the animate nature of the tine wight and is modeled on funeral rites. There are two types:

  • Cremation: Most effective for returning power to the personal sphere of the vitki through the heavenly streams
  • Burial: A powerful way to direct the power through the chthonic streams

2. Ritual Removal of the Runes

This method emphasizes the dynamistic nature of the rune might. The runes are ritually removed from the tine using the knife, and the scrapings are burned in the brazier. This is also a method of banishing the rune magick of another runester.

In all cases, this should be done with simple dignity, attended by proper formalar of the vitki's own composition. Proper respect should be paid to the wight, the rune might, and the shaper of the tine. This "ecology of power" mirrors the ancient Norse lore of rebirth, which postulates that the innate might of the ancestors is continually reformed in the descendants.

Magickal Linkage

Another vital aspect of tine magick is the establishment of a magickal link to the person or thing the taufr is intended to affect. This linkage may be created by attaching a runic formula representing the target, such as a name transliterated into runes, to the object. Physical proximity of the tine to the intended recipient also establishes a connection. Other techniques of sympathetic magick may be employed as well.

Talismanic Construction

Before attempting to construct a runic talisman, the vitki should be well versed in the intellectual content of the rune lore and suitably advanced in the psychic faculties necessary to a successful talismanic operation. Rune tines should be constructed in accordance with the theories and ideology expressed by the runic system to achieve maximal effect.

Materials

  • Wood: Should be of a kind sympathetic to the aim of the talisman. The possibilities are limitless; consult correspondences or let informed intuition guide the selection.
  • Metal: Disks, plates, or rings of copper, bronze, silver, or gold make excellent runic talismans.
  • Stone and Bone: Small, appropriately shaped stones or pieces of bone are also favored. Larger stones serve as stationary talismans; a hammer and chisel dedicated to the runic arts are useful for constructing runestones.
  • Earthenware: Highly receptive to rune loading. Runes may be etched into the finished product or cut into the soft unfired clay, colored properly, and then fired in a ritualistic process of powerful potential.
  • Parchment: Colored with pens, inks, and paints dedicated to ritual practice. Parchment talismans may be carried (in lockets, for example) or serve as stationary symbols.

The imagination of the vitki is the only limit to the possibilities.

Shapes

Certain shapes are best suited to receive runic forms:

  • Rectangular solid
  • Thin wooden stave (1/16 to 1/8 inch thick)
  • Thin disk or rectangular plate
  • Natural tree branch segment
  • Cylindrical shape of various lengths
  • Jewelry of all types
  • Thin rhomboid: A unique and fairly common talismanic shape, usually cut from wood or bone. This form provides four smooth surfaces for longer inscriptions and is extremely convenient and comfortable for tines designed to be carried on the person.

Design Requirements

The main requirement in the external formation of a tine is that it contain:

  1. A symbol or symbols describing the purpose and aims of the talisman
  2. A signature representing the person, persons, or thing to be affected or altered by the force of the first symbol

The signature may be the target's name transliterated into runes, or some other sympathetic link; even physical proximity may serve to form this connection. Space on the object should be aesthetically allocated and divided according to rune staves, holy signs, and the signature. Any combination of these elements is acceptable.

Cutting Technique

The vitki should experiment with various surfaces and tools to determine the best cutting methods for each material. Time invested in the practice of carving runes pays dividends, as greater mechanical skill frees more energy and concentration for the magickal work at hand. One general technique that works well across all material types is the precutting of rune bands: cutting two grooves to act as upper and lower limits for the staves.

Bind Runes

While a tine may express a single runic force, one of the most potent techniques for blending several runic forces together toward a specific purpose is the bind rune (Old Norse bandrún). A bind rune combines individual runic powers into one mighty field of action. This method has the distinct advantage of using only the ideographic essence of the rune, freeing the modern vitki from concerns about linguistic correctness in inscription. To properly build and load such a form, the vitki must possess a deep understanding of the separate runes and how they fit together to produce a single powerful expression of force with a single harmonious will. The principles of spiritual and physical aesthetics are important here.

There are two main types of bandrúnar. The first type connects two or more runes together when inscribing words. This is done to form a magickal link between the runes, to represent two or more words in a coded form, or to reduce the overall count of runes in the inscription. A bind rune always counts as a single rune in the rune count. The common grammatical ending -az (-aR) is frequently written as a bind rune, linking the forces of the A-rune and Z-rune into a special expression. One of the oldest bind runes represents the magickal formula gibu auja (give good luck) and is often carved on talismanic or ritual weapons. Any runes with adjacent vertical staves are prime candidates for binding.

The second type is the purely ideographic bind rune, which may contain a word concealed in its form as a kind of simultaneous anagram. These are the most useful in tine magick, and their multiplicity of levels makes them highly effective in refined operations. A great amount of artistic license is available to the vitki in the construction of bind runes. The alternate forms of the various staves should help in the formation of an aesthetically pleasing shape. When formulating bind runes, the runester should always keep the elements of numerological symbolism and ideological harmony in mind.

One of the oldest examples of an ideographic bind rune is found on the brooch of Soest, dating to approximately 600 to 650 CE. This galdrastafr is a love talisman carved on a brooch and given to a woman. Its power draws upon Ódhinic force combined with justice, a call for success, need (with sexual symbolism), erotic union, and ancestral principles. The rune count and its numerical total emphasize the erotic nature of the talisman. Analysis of old inscriptions such as this provides many clues to modern practice.

Another ideographic example is the "three-headed thurs," essentially a threefold intensification of the Thurisaz rune. This form is used in curses.

Runagaldrar (Runic Incantations)

Poetic runic incantations were a common magickal method. The Poetic Edda, along with numerous runic artifacts, preserves the voice of many ancient incantations.

Stadhagaldr (Posture Magick)

Stadhagaldr is the practice of physically embodying runic forms through posture and incantation. Evidence of this practice appears on the golden drinking horns of Gallehus, which portray humanoid figures striking runic postures as part of magickal formulas. Later Icelandic customs confirm this usage, such as teaching children the alphabet by having them strike a posture resembling each letter.

Magickal Applications

The runes and holy signs serve as focal points for evocatory magick, meditation, self-transmutation, and mystical communication. They are especially potent in workings concerning:

  • Victory and success
  • Protection
  • Rescue from restriction
  • Love
  • The gaining of wisdom

Other Forms of Magick

The runic system encompasses several areas beyond the methods described above. Their scope is vast, and awareness of them opens the door to further exploration.

Oath Magick is bound up with the liturgical forms of Ásatrú. It involves the swearing of oaths upon sacred objects such as the altar ring or a sacrificial animal, channeling binding force through the spoken word and the sanctity of the object.

Invocation and Evocation of gods, goddesses, wights, and aspects of the personal soul may be performed to communicate with the hugr of the vitki. These forms belong more properly to the function of the erilaz, the master of rune lore who works at the highest ceremonial level. Several types of initiation are also proper to the life of the vitki and erilaz.

Seidhr is a magickal form independent of runic symbolism, though it can be woven into the rune world as an integral practice. The Ynglinga Saga recounts how Ódhinn learned the art of seidhr from its mistress, Freyja. Seidhr encompasses shape shifting, soul projection, traveling through the worlds, sex magick, and other techniques that carry what some consider a shamanistic character. The Eddas and sagas offer many inspirational examples for the vitki who wishes to explore these paths.

Tools, Attire & Timing

The "external tools" of rune magick symbolize internal forces. These are the traditional tools and techniques of runagaldr, which aid in the manipulation of the rune streams. For detailed entries on individual tools, see the Materials grimoire.

Attire

The magickal attire of the vitki roughly corresponds to the everyday dress of an early medieval Northman, with special symbolic features. The main advantage of liturgical vestments is the magickal effect of setting oneself apart from everyday life.

An ideal set of ritual attire includes:

  • A hooded cloak or frock of deep blue or black as the outermost piece
  • Bright red pants, a special sign of the vitki in ancient times
  • Black or natural-color heelless leather shoes (though many rites, especially outdoors, should be performed barefoot)
  • A pullover-type tunic of white, blue, or red worn under the cloak, fitting loosely and girdled by a belt of leather or deerskin
  • A sheath for the knife attached to the belt, and a pouch for other magickal instruments

Runes may be represented in the vitki's attire via a white headband embroidered with runes in bright red, and a bracteate engraved with the Futhark row and other magickal symbols (bronze, gold, or silver).

Generally, male and female vitkar dress very much alike; however, the female usually goes bare-legged or wears a long red skirt. Ritual nudity is also practiced according to the nature and aim of the rite. In all matters of magick, let intuition be the primary guide.

Magickal Time

The timing of runic rites is important but not as rigid or complicated as traditions more influenced by zodiacal astrology. The most important criteria are:

  1. Season
  2. Moon phase
  3. Solar position (time of day)

The most auspicious times are dawn, midday, evening, and midnight. For increase of power the waxing moon is desired, but for constriction of force its waning phase is used. The best general time for any undertaking is in the nights of the new moon or just after, or the full moon or just before.

Time and space are considered aspects of one another and both are measured by the mjötvidhr (the measuring tree, Yggdrasill).

Other Ritual Instruments

Several rites require further instruments beyond the primary tools. The cloth, leather thong, and other minor implements are introduced in their pertinent ritual sections.

All major tools needed for the performance of rune work should be portable and so well concealed that no one would even notice their presence. The equipment of the rune vitki is characterized by its mobility.

Rune Storage & Care

How to Store Runes

A set of runes is a small collection of highly magickal objects requiring care and accounting. Treat them as a single entity to avoid incomplete sets.

Multiple Sets Recommended:

  • A sacred set for individual use
  • A travel set you can part with more easily
  • Allows spontaneous "check-in" pulls without risking your primary set

Progression: Start with Witch runes (pictographic, self-explanatory, no transliteration needed), then advance to more esoteric systems like Norse.

Storage by Material:

  • Stone: Store flat in a single layer (box) to prevent scratching. Line lids with soft fabric.
  • Painted staves: Avoid friction to prevent wearing.
  • Witch runes: Small number, usually painted on stones. Cast in a lidded box.
  • Ogham runes: Carved/burned on sticks, require larger surface area for spreads.

Pouch Storage:

  • Drawstring pouches work well. Choose ample size (5" x 7" for most sets).
  • Personalize by embroidering your name in runes (right to left). This creates a bond and accelerates learning.

Environmental Care:

  • Store away from direct light and heat.
  • Sunlight charging is fine occasionally but degrades color saturation over time.
  • Ask sellers if stones are natural, dyed, or heat-treated.

Altar Storage:

  • Arrange runes on altar surface, cover with dedicated cloth.
  • Covering shows respect for the oracle.
  • Do not consult too casually.

Caring for Your Runes

Treat runes as magickal tools, not kitchen utensils.

By Material:

  • Stone: Wrap individually to prevent abrasion and scratching.
  • Wood: Keep clear of candles and oils. Prevent dust accumulation.
  • Metal Runes: Store airtight to prevent oxidation. Dark patina is not necessarily undesirable.

General Practice:

  • Consult runes in ritual (need not be elaborate).
  • Enter expanded consciousness with intentional receptivity.
  • Consider: cloth pouch color, box type, storage location. All impact effectiveness.

Treatment Cautions:

  • Essential Oils: Can dissolve painted staves. Discolors wood permanently. Only use on carved/burned staves with awareness of effects.
  • Salt/Salt Water: Corrosive. Rinse briefly rather than soak. Never submerge wood (warps, splits, damages).
  • Sunlight/Smoke: Will impact appearance over time.

Signing, Sending & Protection

Signing and Sending of Runes

The practice of making runic gestures or signs was well known in ancient times. The Norse godhar (priests) would make the "sign of the hammer" (Old Norse hamarsmark) over goblets before drinking. This rite was established well before the coming of Christianity.

How to Sign a Rune

A rune may be traced in the air with:

  • The palm of the right hand
  • The right index finger
  • The right thumb
  • The rune wand

Some staves may be signed with both hands in a smooth and aesthetic gesture.

Visualization and Projection

The vitki should project the image of the stave from a sphere of brightness in the center of the body, along a shaft of red light to the point where the rune is intended to appear. Once the beam has reached this distance, trace the form of the stave from the substance of light. The color may be red or some other symbolic hue.

Breath Rhythm

  1. Inhale as the arm is raised, concentrating on the intake of önd
  2. Exhale, sending and signing the stave while singing the name and/or galdr of the rune

After the Signing

The invoked force may be:

  • Reabsorbed into the personal sphere of the runester
  • Infused into an object as an act of loading or "charging"
  • Sent to do work elsewhere

This is one of the most powerful techniques available to the vitki, but one that must be mastered with extremely strong concentration and visualization.

Rituals of Protection

Before beginning any ceremonial rune work, the vitki should perform a rite that banishes all forces detrimental to the work at hand. These forces are not "evil," merely disadvantageous to the operation.

Three formulas serve this purpose:

  1. The Hammer Rite (Hamarssetning): The strongest, providing maximal protection and isolation
  2. The Hagalaz Rite: Provides the most potent magickal atmosphere and potential
  3. The Elhaz Rite: Strikes a balance between protection and magickal potency

A rite of this type may be practiced every day and should be used in conjunction with an opening ritual to begin all ceremonial work.

Galdr & Sign Magick

A galdr is a magick song in which runes are sung. Giving voice to something amplifies it, creating a vibrational link between the witch and the rune while engaging with the space-time continuum to affect outcomes.

Galdr (Magick Song)

Historical Origins

Also called a shield song, galdr was historically used to affect battle outcomes. It was meant to be amplified, a sound intended to carry, whether to inspire, intimidate, bind, or defeat.

The technique involved singing at very high pitch and loud volume. Warriors positioned shields over their mouths to create resonance as sound waves bounced off metal surfaces, dramatically increasing projection.

Traditional Uses

  • Battle: Shifting conflict energy into victory
  • Healing: Chanted repeatedly at the bedside of the afflicted
  • Cursing: Directing harmful energy toward targets
  • Divination: Summoning spirits who could bring knowledge of the future

The Hand-Cupping Method

Hold your hands together, slightly cupped, about 2-3 inches from your mouth. This creates a resonating chamber that directs sound back to your own ears. The power may be surprising at first.

This technique works well in coven settings, those hesitant to engage with their power publicly can benefit from the modesty that covering the mouth allows.

How to Perform a Galdr

  1. Choose your rune: Select from your cast or choose one aligned with your intended outcome
  2. Position: Use the hand-cupping method or hold your altar charger in front of your nose and mouth
  3. Face your altar and close your eyes
  4. Visualize: Envision the best possible outcome for everyone involved
  5. Sing: Voice your rune with as much power as you can muster

The Nature of the Sound

The song does not have to be pretty. It is not a performance. It can be primal, guttural, or transcendent, whatever your spirit needs in that moment. The sound may waver from a cry to a shriek to a cackle.

There is no wrong way to sing a galdr as long as you put your heart and soul into it and make certain the sound is loud and clear.

Why It Works

Using a galdr is a form of invocation. Invoking powers to come to your aid increases energy and improves outcomes. Bringing this practice from the distant past and reinterpreting it for modern use is a form of reconstruction, the human need for protection, healing, and manifestation remains unchanged.

Sign Magick (Signingagaldr)

Signingagaldr blends the techniques of signing and sending with galdr (incantation). This form of magick is the most difficult because it requires the greatest concentration and visualization to be maximally effective. Once the techniques have been mastered, however, it promises to be the most direct and effective form of galdr available to the vitki.

The main difference between signing in this context and that used in the loading of tines is that here the signs are directed toward and melded with already living systems, whether wights or dynamistic fields of runic force.

The Principle

The vitki cuts runes into the living fabric of the multiverse, melding rune might with a symbolic "target" formulated by the hugr through concentrated visualization, bringing about a change in that target. This is only one of many ways to use sign magick techniques. The process may be carried out in the hugauga (totally by meditative visualization) or by external ritual work. In both cases the techniques are the same, though the vitki may wish to begin with visualization and work into more difficult ceremonial performance.

The Three Steps of Signingagaldr

  1. Formulation of and/or concentration on a target
  2. Formulation and projection of the willed rune might
  3. Melding of the previous two into a single field of force such that the second influences the first in the desired way

Formulating a Target

To formulate a target for the projected magickal force, the vitki sets off a "target area": a framework within which the visualized target is held, so that the rune might may be directed into it. This may be rectangular or triangular in shape.

In full ritual work, a frame may be constructed from wood and suitably painted or decorated. The frame may contain a symbolic form of the target (a picture, for example), but most often the vitki will magickally build the form of the target image within the framework using powers of concentration and visualization.

Projection and Melding

Once the target is firmly established and bound within the frame, the vitki begins to formulate the willed rune might in the center of the body. This power is then projected into the target area and signed in the manner of sending and signing. The galdr and/or formali that is sung or spoken gives intention and refined form to the runic power. As the vitki signs the rune, the force of the sign should feel as if it is actually being infused into the living fabric of the target. The vitki will immediately perceive the change in the target once the melding of forces is complete.

The Role of Galdr in Sign Magick

Both sound-formulaic and poetic forms of galdrar may be used, but the vitki should always aim for the more complex poetic form because of the degree of flexibility and exactness it affords. These magick songs are found throughout old Germanic literatures. For the ancient Germanic peoples, the art of poetry grew out of the power of magick.

The galdr serves to aid in the invocation and evocation of the rune might and in its formation within the vitki. It also aids in projection and linkage of that force to the target through its principal quality: vibration.

Breath and Concentration

The breath should be the focal point of concentration throughout the galdr. During inhalations, the vitki concentrates on the flow of rune might into the personal center. There it is momentarily held for exact formulation, and then on exhalation, the portion of the galdr to be projected is intensely concentrated on.

Most galdrar require several breaths to perform completely. One line of the incantation may be performed with each breath. In the case of poetic galdrar, the vitki should "runically" concentrate on each letter-sound of every word in the incantation, feeling their force rather than thinking about their meaning. If well composed, the galdr will seem to do its own work. What is important is the flow of force, its formulation, and its projection in a smooth concentrated pattern that becomes almost unconscious to the accomplished vitki. A unity is built between the rune might, the vitki, and the target.

Sound and Form

The main magickal unity on which the vitki must consciously concentrate is that of the sound (of the incantation) and the form (of the stave and the beam of light through which it is projected), all within the common "runic vibration." Meditational exercises will greatly aid in this process.

Incantations may be sung either out loud or within the hugr. When spoken aloud, galdrar may be sonorously and boomingly sung or softly whispered. The former seems more effective when the vitki performs in solitude or in the company of fellow vitkar, while the latter is often more powerful when non-vitkar are present.

Preparation

Because this form of galdr comes so close to an unconscious, meditational approach, it is essential to memorize all aspects of the rite before performance. A successful work of signingagaldr depends on a magnificent blend of all segments of the vitki's psychosomatic complex. The unexpected mystical results of these operations are often astounding.

On Composing Poetic Galdrar

Poetic galdrar may certainly be composed in the vitki's native language. Much thought should go into their composition as to both form and content. The dedicated vitki will undertake the study of Old Norse and/or other old Germanic dialects (Old English, Gothic, Old High German), for these languages vibrate with magicko-mythic qualities that are difficult to conjure in modern tongues. Most important is that the vitki finds a magickally potent language and poetic form that speaks with the voice of the unconscious realms.

Stadhagaldr (Posture Magick)

Stadhagaldr is an active system of magick consisting of the assumption of runic postures or gestures for magickal effect, both within the vitki and in the surrounding environment. It most likely shares a common Indo-European root tradition of magickal and symbolic gestures with other systems of sacred posture work.

Gestures and postures form part of almost every metaphysical or magickal school, from the simple folding of hands in prayer to extremely complex systems of physical practice. Stadhagaldr is balanced in this respect: the number and intricacy of the postures are varied enough to express the wide variety of forces present, but none require extensive training or straining of the body.

The great advantage of stadhagaldr within the runic system is that it allows the actual shape of the stave to be embodied in the physical apparatus of the vitki. This can result in the embodiment of the entire runic mystery in the flesh, turning the body into a powerful magickal tool.

The Six Aims of Stadhagaldr

Each aim should be striven for in turn, until all six have been mastered:

  1. Control of the body through posture (stadha)
  2. Control of thought through song (galdr)
  3. Control of breath
  4. Control of emotion
  5. Becoming aware of the rune realms of the self and of the world(s)
  6. Control and direction of the will

The Body as Magickal Instrument

The body should not be viewed as something to be defeated or forced into submission but rather as a source of great and holy energy, obtainable through no other medium, when directed in harmony with the hugr. The body is the vitki's personal portion of Midhgardhr, the balanced center of the multiverse containing the potential of all the worlds.

Applications

Stadhagaldr serves as a mode of psychological integration and personal transmutation, and it is also employed in all other types of magickal operations. The vitki may literally build a numinous, living runic talisman within the body through stadhagaldr, becoming a walking rune line. The principles of runic combination and blending work with stadhagaldr in exactly the same way they function with tine or sign magick. The stödhur are simply an alternate mode of expression for the rune might.

Intake of World and Earth Streams

The practice of stadhagaldr is closely connected to the mysteries of the rune streams. The runic postures act as antennas of force by which the vitki may attract, modulate, and re-project rune might for magickal purposes.

There are three types of rune streams:

  • Heavenly streams: Cosmic forces from above, not peculiar to this planet
  • Terrestrial streams: Flow just under and above the surface of the earth, specific to this planet
  • Subterranean (chthonic) streams: Cosmic forces from below, not peculiar to this planet

The individual self contains counterparts to each of these streams, which act as a matrix through which the rune streams act upon and affect the vitki. These streams are perceived in many different ways: some as vibrations, others as waves, flows, rays, and even contractions. The induction of these forces is the mainstay of stadhagaldr.

How Force Flows

Power is drawn in through the hands, feet, and head, directly to the central axis of the vitki. There it is absorbed and modulated, then reemitted for specific purposes or assimilated to alter the self. Each runic posture receives and transmits force in a particular pattern, and from various realms, according to its shape.

This power is directly connected to the physical world through the medium of the human nervous system. When performing the various rune stödhur, the vitki should visualize and feel the flows of force being gathered or projected in a particular pattern through the body, which is in the form of the stave. This will feel as if electric current is passing through the body and will appear as rays of light coursing in angular patterns.

Personal experience should always take precedence. Personal feelings and reactions, rather than "logical" thought processes, are more effective guidelines in the realm of practical magick. This is especially true in stadhagaldr.

Patterns of Force Streams

Four general patterns illustrate how the streams interact with the body during posture work. The arrows indicate the directions in which force streams, though these should not be taken as dogma:

Chthonic circulation: Subterranean streams are lifted into the vitki and circulate back to their source

Synthesis and manifestation: Heavenly and subterranean forces flow into the vitki, are synthesized, and sent out into the terrestrial realm as manifest action

Crosscurrent intensification: A crosscurrent of directed terrestrial force flows through the vertical axis of world streams, resulting in a concentrated intensification of power at the point of confluence

Heavenly redirection: Heavenly and subterranean streams are received and assimilated, then all are redirected toward the heavenly realm

The diagonals sometimes feel like terrestrial links and sometimes like links to the heavenly or subterranean realms. This is true even with the same rune on different occasions, for the rune world is hardly static. A skilled vitki will attempt to experience all of these forces empirically, then begin to divide and classify the raw forces into their finer runic characteristics.

Power Points and Preparation

The ancient vitkar knew well the power of the earth streams, for they formed one of their mightiest mysteries. The best work-stead for stadhagaldr is a known "power point" where the earth and world streams (the horizontal and vertical) flow together. These are recognized by all cultures across the world, and the vitki should seek them out for important rites of stadhagaldr.

The human being is constantly bombarded by power flowing from above, below, and from all corners of the earth. The task is to control this influx and direct it. The power of brightness is received from the wide expanse of space, and the constricting force of darkness is inducted from the center of the earth. It is vital to realize both extremes, consciously seek them out, develop them to their limits, and center them in consciousness.

Before attempting any practical magickal work in this system, the stödhur of all the runes to be used in the operation should be mastered through an intense program of meditational exercise with the runic postures in question.

Opening Formula (Stadhasetning)

A work of stadhagaldr may begin with the general opening rite used in talismanic magick, or the vitki may use a special stadhasetning (posture rite) for engaging the runic forces. This is a powerful rite with which to practice stadhagaldr, and therefore these three stödhur should perhaps be mastered first.

When a stave is presented beside a galdr formali, it indicates that the vitki should assume the stadha of the rune and sing its formulaic galdr and/or the formali that loads the ritual actions with more refined intentions.

The Three Stödhur for Engaging Runic Forces

First Stadha:

for beams and waves of rune might.

Second Stadha:

from the deepest depths

Third Stadha:

Simple Rites

The performance of any single rune stadha may be considered a rite, especially if the vitki composes a formali to be recited after the galdr is sung. This formali gives specific shape and purpose to the runic force engendered by the operation. The possibilities for potent works of simple beauty are almost limitless.

The following rites of combined runic forces are made up of several simpler rites blended together to form more complex magickal effects. They describe flows or processes of power aimed toward a specific goal. The advantage of stadha-ritual work is that it provides keys to various realms of consciousness and inspires the vitki to the greatest power, if properly performed on all levels of being.

The aim in the rites of stadhagaldr is the blending of several runic forces into one single concentrated and directed stream of power with a definite goal. This is achieved by combining the forms and sounds of various runes together into a single force field of action. The symbol of the operation may be a series of runes or a bind rune drawn on the floor, on a board lying on the altar, or hung at eye level on the wall in front of the vitki. This form should be the focal point of concentration throughout the entire ritual.

These ritual formulas may also be adapted as talismanic or sign-magickal rites.

The Ritual Talisman

Whether or not the vitki is performing a talismanic loading ritual, a symbol describing the particular runic operation may be formed to serve as a lasting outward symbol of the holy inner process that takes place in the rite. This is usually a bind rune or rune row, incised into or painted on a board or paper. It should be displayed where the vitki will see it regularly, constantly reaffirming the link to the magickal force. It may also be portrayed on a small object the vitki carries.

This technique should be used only when the vitki desires to effect an internal change in consciousness. For operations intended to affect the outside environment, the vitki should expend all possible energy during the ritual, then make a complete break with the force, releasing it to do its work. In the latter case, a constant reminder would only hinder the successful fulfillment of the vitki's will.

Runic Communication & Expression

Because runes are alphabetic, it is entirely possible to transliterate using runes. Communication is key to any successful relationship, giving voice to one's own needs comes with a certain amount of risk. Some risks are worth taking, but it is often impossible to know from the outset how things are likely to progress.

This is where runes become invaluable. By creating a bind-rune, you signal your intention and inject energy into the field of perceptible energy.

Communicating a Need

Step 1: Dialogue with Yourself

Identify one specific need or requirement and focus only on that. Draw the characters from your preferred rune system.

Can you name what you need in the simplest terms? Can you simplify what you need into a single word?

Consider the dimensions of your life:

  • Family
  • Community ties
  • Love and relationships
  • Hobbies
  • Spirituality
  • Future goals
  • Past debts

Think about what drives you and what constrains you. Choose one, either a motivating factor or a constraint, and refine it into a single word.

Example words: Time, Health, Love, Travel, Work, Wealth, Study

These words are intentionally short because your next step will be to express them along a single stave.

Creating a Communication Stave

Draw a single vertical line in the middle of a blank grimoire page. If using Ogham runes, start from the bottom and work up, transliterating into your mother tongue.

Example Process:

ElementContent
ThoughtI need more time to accomplish my goals
IntentionGoal (be specific: clairvoyance, mediumship, good grades, new job)
ConstraintTime

External and Metaphysical Communication

After establishing dialogue with yourself, the next level is external and metaphysical, engaging with spirit, ancestor, deity, or the source of power connected to your modern practice.

Steps for Formal Request:

  1. Identify and name the metaphysical level of communication (specific deity, name of ancestor, elemental energy)
  2. Establish connection using a tool (mantra, galdr, pendulum, spirit board)
  3. Make a formal request for aid, insight, or prophecy

Once intention and tools are ready, silently focus on the stave while invoking metaphysical energy.

A Note on Time

Albert Einstein proved that time is relative, the rate at which time passes is connected to your frame of reference. Einstein argued that time is an illusion and that the separation of past, present, and future is not set.

Remember the truth about gravity, space, and the passage of time, and accept your own ability to exercise flexibility when manipulating time.

Runes as Body Adornment

Just as you can consecrate a candle using runes, you can apply the same technique to your physical person.

Invisible Intention Work

If you want to inspire sexy confidence, use your favorite essential oil blend to write your desires in runes on your own body. These intentions will not be visible to anyone, but you will know they are there.

Even a simple transliteral rune for "touch" or "kiss" traced with your fingertip up and down your arms and legs, or "hold" on your hand, will prepare your body and mind to welcome sensuality.

Visible Adornment

If outward expression feels right to you, liquid eyeliner can prove to be a useful medium for adorning the body with runes.

Invisible Application Methods

If visibility is not something you are ready for yet, or if you are less inclined toward formal anointing with essential oil blends, you can also use:

  • Moisturizer
  • Foundation

These invisible but powerful gestures become part of your physical makeup and add a layer of magick to your grooming.

Rune Grimoire

Divination & Casting

Historical Roots of Runic Divination

Divination is among the oldest applications of the runes. Runic forms were carved into pieces of wood, cast onto a white cloth, and interpreted according to strict criteria. The Roman historian Tacitus documented this practice among the continental Germanic peoples in the first century CE, describing it as a fully developed divinatory rite. The runes used for divination were not separate from the magickal system; the same symbols that encoded sacred mysteries also served as oracular tools.

The Tacitus Method (Hlutfall)

Tacitus documented this ancient lot-casting technique in the Germania, and it remains one of the most accessible entry points for the modern vitki. The method requires twenty-four rune lots (hlutar) ritually constructed from oak or beech wood, each loaded with a different stave of the Elder Futhark. Flat, thin strips of veneer roughly one inch by two inches work well. A white linen cloth approximately three feet square is also needed.

At an auspicious time, preferably outdoors, spread the cloth on the ground with its flat edges aligned to the four quarters. Stand near the southern edge facing north and shuffle the lots while concentrating on the subject of inquiry. Hold the lots in both hands, assume the stadha, and fix the mind firmly on the question. Once a strong link has formed, sing the galdr:

Rúnar rádha rátt rádh!

(Runes rown right rede!)

Then cast the lots onto the cloth, calling the Nornic names before they land:

Urdhr, Verdhandi, Skuld!

Close the eyes and walk to the cloth. Randomly pick up three lots. The first reveals the past or root of the matter, the second illuminates the present condition, and the third indicates what should come about given the other two factors. Further insight into this technique may be drawn from the mysteries of Pertho.

Casting Methods

The method you choose depends on preference, spread type, and the energetic principles at play. The most appropriate cast aligns oracle, caster, and question.

Random Pull:

  • Draw from pouch or box array.
  • Liberating when confronting things beyond your control.
  • Relinquishing control diminishes ego, strengthens oracular connection.
  • Brings immediate peace to chaotic situations.

Deliberate Pull:

  • Use when a situation requires reigning in.
  • Controlled spread for focused inquiry.

Neither technique has value over the other. Match method to energetic context.

Developing Psychic Abilities

Divination ("seeing beyond") is both talent and skill.

  • Talent: Inherent aptitude that waxes and wanes based on nurturing.
  • Skill: Developed through intentional practice.

Key Principle: Repetition alone is insufficient. Repetition must be accompanied by clear intention to improve. Repeating mistakes creates neurological pathways for error.

Strengthening Techniques

1. Visualization

Learn to see beyond what eyes perceive or mind imagines.

Progression:

  1. Visualize familiar objects in excruciating detail (color, shape, texture, dimension, light reflection).
  2. Add sensory layers: temperature, scent.
  3. Increase complexity: count lotus petals, notice color gradations.
  4. Apply to known memories with full detail.
  5. Apply to emotions.
  6. Apply to unknowns you can verify (e.g., rooms in a friend's home).
  7. Visualize runes: trace staves mentally, listen for their sounds and messages.

2. Meditation

Quiet the mind. Create room for psychic awareness by emptying mundane thoughts.

  • Center consciousness on body and breath.
  • Focus on energy exchange with environment.
  • Start small. Racing thoughts are normal at first.

Important: Relaxation is a by-product, not the goal. Meditative awareness is heightened, not lessened. It should feel enlivening, not sleep-inducing.

3. Opening the Mind

An open mind is accepting, able to entertain possibilities, and able to receive. Requires confronting inherent biases and maintaining unattachment to outcomes.

When runes challenge you:

  • Examine if you hoped for something you did not see.
  • Sit with uncomfortable information.
  • Disturbing messages are not guarantees of disaster.
  • Warnings can lead you in the right direction.

Aura Exercise

Once each skill is developed in isolation, combine them:

  1. Meditate: Comfortable seated position. Breathe from diaphragm. Close eyes. Focus on breath.
  2. Mantra: Use a single rune name or bindrune pronunciation to center focus.
  3. Visualize aura: Picture it as a second skin of light. Notice color gradations and temperature.
  4. Extend aura: Project it outward to touch the unseen. Reach in all directions.
  5. Receive: Listen for temperature changes, visions, information coming through the projected field.
  6. Return: Call aura back. Return to present moment.

Preparing Your Space

Preparation is necessary. A casual preparation yields casual results.

Choose Comfort:

  • Physical discomfort draws focus from reading.
  • Grounding (floor, outdoors) is fine if comfortable.
  • Use a cleared table or altar with appealing chair or mat.

Remove Distractions:

  • Face away from clocks
  • Shut down computers
  • Silence phones
  • Create stillness

Consecrate the Space:

  • Make a declaration (silent or spoken) that you are entering sacred space.
  • Use a dedicated cloth, handled as valuable.
  • Light candles as beacons for insight.
  • Perform smoke clearing with burned herbs.
  • Keep grimoire nearby for recording.
  • A dish of salt, stick of incense, cup of water, and candle create a hearth for communion.

Preparing Yourself

  1. Hold runes (in pouch or box) at heart level, eyes closed.
  2. Feel heartbeat creating vibrational link to corporeal body.
  3. Breathe into the vibration. Focus on breath and heartbeat.
  4. Let everything else fall away.
  5. When mind is clear, touch the runes.

Asking the Question

Formulate clearly:

  • Begin with a single question (multiple questions obscure which part runes respond to).
  • Use open-ended words: "what" or "which."
  • Examples: "What is the likely result if I choose [scenario]?" or "Which course of action leads to [desired outcome]?"

Speak aloud:

  • Runes are a language. Query must travel vibrationally.
  • Silent queries can indicate distrust or "testing" the oracle.
  • Skepticism yields less accurate readings.
  • Words create change: speaking creates sound wave frequencies; writing creates enduring physical transformation.

Harnessing Energy

Three Methods:

  1. Pull/Draw: Deliberate. Best for clarity and choice.
  2. Toss/Throw: Chaotic. Best when stuck and needing direction.
  3. Swirl: Invokes change.

Swirl Technique:

  • Place runes facedown on smooth surface.
  • Cover with both hands.
  • Left hand clockwise, right hand counterclockwise.
  • Allow runes to "escape" between hands.
  • Stop when runes feel ready or spontaneously turn over.

Pull vs. Draw (Energetic Distinction)

  • Pull: Rune calling to you. Active. Engages the heart. Domain of experience.
  • Draw: You calling to rune. Subtle. Engages the mind. Domain of knowledge.

When to Pull vs. Throw

Practical Considerations:

  • Glass runes: Never throw (will chip).
  • Ogham sticks: Satisfying to toss.
  • Heavy stone runes: Too heavy to throw.
  • Ceramic: Can pull or toss.

Energetic Considerations:

  • Focused state but need to feel unbridled: Use random method.
  • Chaotic energy but need focus: Choose deliberately one by one.

The Six Steps of Rune Casting

  1. Preparation: Physical and emotional space. Variable: Surroundings and needs.
  2. Query: Open-ended question. Variable: Spoken, written, or both.
  3. Cast: Total number of runes. Variable: Pull, throw, or turn.
  4. Spread: Arrangement. Variable: Relates to depth of question.
  5. Interpretation: Reading. Variable: Modern or traditional meanings.
  6. Reflection: Integrating new information. Variable: Recorded or ephemeral.

Memorize these steps. As you become adept, you will learn which parts can be truncated.

Rune Sticks

Historical Discovery

In 1954 near Greenland's southernmost point, the Narsaq stick was discovered among textiles, bone fragments, and caribou antler tools, a pine stick carved with Norse runes never before seen in Greenland. This marked the first evidence of a Norse settlement there.

Four rune sticks total were found, bearing the Futhark in short twig form. Though carved by different individuals, their purpose appears consistent: magick and cipher. One interpretation suggests a prayer for safe sea passage; another appears to be a riddle or coded message.

Practical Applications

Talismans and Charms:

  • Carve or draw an intention on a stick
  • Carry it with you or wear on your person
  • Works with both Norse and Ogham runes

Spell Components:

  • Incorporate rune sticks into spell jars
  • Use as part of larger magickal workings

Casting with Rune Sticks

Rune sticks can be cast similarly to Witch runes:

  1. Enliven with friction: Roll sticks back and forth between your palms
  2. Release: Allow them to fall naturally
  3. Interpret position and relationship:
    • Which runes face you?
    • Which are close together?
    • Which are distant?
    • Which sticks are touching?

The spatial relationships guide your reading, adding a dimension beyond traditional spread positions.

Accepting Outcomes

Divination is an art, and practitioners sometimes reveal what they'd rather not know. Any predictive endeavor carries risk to the status quo.

Key Principles:

  • All participants retain free agency and personal will
  • A bad omen does not equate with a bad outcome
  • Warnings can be the impetus needed to ward off larger disaster
  • Short-term sacrifice is often necessary
  • Ordeals are native to rune work

Growth Through Acceptance:

Embracing the full range of human experience cultivates compassion, ethics, and openness.

Yes, openness carries danger, but runes are also linked to protective magick. Mastering multiple applications leaves practitioners feeling empowered rather than vulnerable.

Accepting an undesirable outcome is not the same as invoking it. You can always avoid sailing directly into the storm if you have the courage to take the helm and direct your journey via a safer passage.

Rune Spreads

A rune spread interprets selected runes in a specific order. Spreads range from simple check-ins to in-depth examinations. Each selection and placement carries distinct significance.

Getting Started

  1. Formulate a question: Make it specific but open-ended (avoid yes/no questions). Address the oracle directly as a source of power.
  2. Set the tone: Approach the runes with seriousness and respect, but maintain joy in your heart.
  3. Prepare: Clear your mind and eliminate distractions.

Single-Rune Spread

This is the simplest method for quick engagement.

  1. Stillness: Take a moment to center yourself.
  2. Focus: Speak your question aloud over the runes.
  3. Draw: Choose a single rune without looking.

Use for:

  • Daily focus
  • Checking the energy of a situation
  • Identifying immediate obstacles or influences

Three-Rune Spread

A spread for deeper insight, often referencing the Triple Goddess or the flow of time. Draw three runes and place them from right to left.

1. Right (The Present/You):

Represents your current state and what you need to hear right now.

2. Center (The Inner/Emotion):

Reveals your internal emotional landscape. Meditate on this rune for clarity on your feelings.

3. Left (The External/Environment):

Shows outside influences and how others see the situation. Guides your next steps.

Five-Rune Spread

Based on the pentagram and the connection of mind, body, and spirit.

1. Top (Head): You in the present situation.

2. Right (Left Hand): The obstacle or focus, what you must take in hand.

3. Bottom Left (Left Foot): The past events leading to this moment.

4. Bottom Right (Right Foot): The next step you must take.

5. Left (Right Hand): The near-term future or what is within reach.

(Note: Directional instructions are sunwise/clockwise).

Ten-Rune Spread

A pyramid-shaped spread for deep psychological dives and complex queries.

Layer 1 (Bottom, 4 Runes): Foundation & Future

Read right to left:

  1. Distant past influence
  2. Recent past influence
  3. Near future influence
  4. Far future implications

Layer 2 (Middle, 3 Runes): The Present

The standard three-rune spread (You, Inner Emotion, External Influence).

Layer 3 (Top, 2 Runes): Guidance

  1. The obstacle
  2. The solution or way to integrate the obstacle

Capstone (Topmost, 1 Rune): Outcome

The final culmination of the reading.

Keep a journal of your spreads. Runes are mysterious, and meanings often clarify over time.

Ogham-Specific Spreads

Since Ogham is a tree oracle and calendar system, casting requires attunement to nature and time.

Preparation & Timing

  • Connection: Connect with tree archetypes like Dryads (female tree spirits) or the Green Man. Best consulted outdoors.
  • Moon Phases:
    • Waxing/Full: For beginnings and new endeavors.
    • Waning/New: For closure and endings.

Ogham Three-Rune Spread (Seasonal)

Use this spread to determine the timing and duration of events.

  1. Rune 1 (The Season/Inception): Reveals the time of year the situation began.
  2. Rune 2 (Duration): Indicates how long the effects will last or the time required to prepare for the next phase.
  3. Rune 3 (Resolution): Forecasts the time of year when the energy will shift, loose ends will tie up, or completion will occur.

Ogham Five-Rune Spread (Vertical Line)

This spread uses a vertical alignment, mirroring the traditional orientation of Ogham script.

Layout: Place runes in a vertical line from bottom to top.

  1. Position 1 (Bottom): Distant past or past life influences.
  2. Position 2 (Below Center): Recent past influences just behind you.
  3. Position 3 (Center, First Drawn): Represents The Self and your present state of mind.
  4. Position 4 (Above Center): Near future influences (within the calendar year).
  5. Position 5 (Top): Distant future consequences (beyond the present year).

Ogham Ten-Rune Spread (Star/Circle)

Modeled after medieval star motifs, this complex spread examines the psyche and situation from all angles.

Layout:

  1. Center: The Self in the present moment.
  2. Crosses Center: The Obstacle or Challenge.
  3. Above Center: Highest hopes, desire, and best possible outcome.
  4. Below Center: Action to take or energy leading to the outcome.
  5. Right: External influences (Family, Community, Connections).
  6. Left: Inner emotions and internal state of balance.
  7. Northeast (between 3 & 5): Weakness to address.
  8. Southeast (between 4 & 5): Outward appearance and surrounding environmental energy.
  9. Southwest (between 4 & 6): Rune of Strength.
  10. Northwest (between 6 & 3): Future influences manifesting from the present course.

Sigil & Manifestation Techniques

Runes have magickal applications beyond divination. As symbols of power, they can protect, attract, or repel. One early use was labeling: carving "candle" in runes on a candle infuses it with mystery and importance.

Runes for Manifesting and Invoking

Using runes as mantras or spoken during spells sharpens focus and intention. You are creating a new reality according to your will.

Three Key Norse Runes:

  1. Mannaz (Self):
    • Represents the self, self-care, self-empowerment.
    • Belief in your own abilities.
    • Notice: Jēra and Kaunaz patterns are contained within Mannaz. Everything you need already dwells within you.
  2. Jēra (Harvest/Abundance):
    • Having enough. You define what "enough" means.
    • Sustenance, rewards of hard work.
    • Can signify time, material comfort, money, wealth, or all three.
  3. Kaunaz (Transformational Opening):
    • Not just fire, but an opening that can grow if properly tended.
    • Use to create openings in the field of dreams.

Inverted Triangle Formation

For manifesting (not divination), you choose runes consciously with clear intention. Manifest within one year or the current Wheel of the Year.

Layout:

  • Point (bottom): Mannaz
  • Upper right: Jēra
  • Upper left: Kaunaz

Practice:

  1. Enter trancelike state while gazing on the formation.
  2. You (Mannaz) are the foundation.
  3. Jēra makes your desire visible, tangible, observable.
  4. Kaunaz sets it in motion.

Why Inverted Triangle: Creates a visual vessel/funnel for focus. Alchemical symbol for water, which flows with great force, cannot be contained but can be channeled.

Action Required: Spoken charms and trance alone are insufficient. The confluence of intention AND action creates the opening.

Rune Stacking (Cairn Method)

Stacking differs from casting: you intentionally choose specific runes to activate outcomes. Stack tiles, wood slices, or balance sticks.

Cairn Symbolism:

  • Used by travelers to guide others
  • Directs unseen energies
  • Signals commitment to your path
  • Temporary; dismantle when blessing manifests

Stack Order (bottom to top):

  1. Mannaz (bottom): Core of your being
  2. Kaunaz (middle): The opening
  3. Jēra (top): Abundance flowing through

Mantra:

Jēra, Abundance!
Kaunaz, Opening!
Mannaz, All flows to me!

The cairn is a guidepost reminding you to act in accord.

Vertical Axis Stacking (Card Method)

Draw the stack on cardboard the size of a business/credit card. This follows the Golden Mean ratio, found in nature and architecture, inherently pleasing and carries divine patterns.

Placement Options:

  • Altar: For ongoing work
  • Wallet: For money/wealth manifestation
  • Pocket/shoe: For healing/health
  • Under pillow: For dream manifestation
  • Gift to others: For manifesting on their behalf

Stacking with Ogham Runes

Ogham runes share a common stave, making them ideal for stacking.

  1. Take credit-card-sized cardboard.
  2. Draw vertical line lengthwise through middle.
  3. One side: Esoteric stack (e.g., Duir for strength, Gort for flowering, Coll for wisdom).
  4. Other side: Transliterate your single-word intention.

Note: Ogham staves read bottom to top.

Creating Sigils with Runes

Sigils are deeply personal. Though runes are recognizable, a sigil's meaning is for the creator alone. Used on magick coins, squares, and amulets, sigils unite practitioners with celestial energy.

What is a Sigil: A monogram of overlapping letters within a circle or square, creating a new distinct character. The act of creation imbues it with magickal energy.

Core Components:

  1. Sound: Audible vibrational energy
  2. Character: Unique visual pattern
  3. Idea: The magickal mind's imagining
  4. Actual representation: The witch's ability to see beyond

Example Sigils (Combining Systems)

Each sigil contains a guide function: the pictographic element shows what you want; the transliteration shows what action to take.

1. Success/Harvest Sigil:

  • Center: Witch rune for Harvest (inscribed in circle)
  • Above: "REAP" transliterated right-to-left: Perthro, Ansuz, Ehwaz, Raidō

2. Truth/Seeing Sigil:

  • Center: Witch rune for Eye (inscribed in circle)
  • Above: "TRUTH" transliterated right-to-left
  • Use when someone is not forthright

3. Bonding Sigil:

  • Center: Witch rune of Rings (inscribed in circle)
  • Outer rings: First initials of both people
  • Center ring: Bindrune combining both initials

Materials: Cardstock, air-drying clay with scribe, or record in grimoire.

Protective Rune Sigils

Runes were frequently used in instruments of battle, emblazoned on shields, helmets, blades, and hilts. The awe they inspire aids the bearer with both power and protection.

The Psychology of Runic Protection

Fear arises when confronting the unfamiliar or unknown. This works in the rune bearer's favor. In accordance with Newton's third law: for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Any blow is absorbed by its target and changed by it.

The Aegishjalmr (Helm of Awe)

This spiked, rayed motif carries the power of invincibility from the Northern Tradition.

  • Aegis - Old Norse for "shield," synonymous with protection
  • Hjalmr - "Helm," meaning a position of responsibility, authority, and high visibility

Core Elements:

  • A central circle
  • Eight rays beginning at center and extending beyond the circle
  • Elhaz (Algiz) - for layered protection
  • Isa - to "freeze" enemies and render them incapable of attack

Modern Applications: Confrontations, negotiations, court proceedings, online interactions, relationships with power differentials.

Working with the Helm:

  1. Trace the symbol on your forehead
  2. Visualize radiating vanquishing power from the center
  3. See the power gain strength as it travels down the staves
  4. Push outward in any direction, as far and forcefully as needed

Apotropaic Runes

Like the Vegvísir, the Aegishjalmr provides both strength and protection through:

  • Repeating staves
  • Star motifs centered around a common intersecting point

Using Bindrunes: Combine runes for specific purposes. For victory, combine Nauthiz stave (need) + Teiwaz apex (victory) = "I am in need of victory."

Creating Personal Rune Staves

Determining Your Number:

  1. Add all numbers in your birth date
  2. Continue adding digits until you reach a single number under 10
  3. This determines the number of staves in your protection symbol

Construction Process:

  1. Use a circle template to locate the center point
  2. Mark vertical and horizontal half-circle points
  3. Divide equally based on your stave number
  4. Choose your rune system
  5. Repeat the pattern evenly along each ray

Ordeals and Obstacles

Odin discovered runes through ordeal. Hardship is inescapable; magick is used to confront, integrate, dispel, or transform constraints.

When Negative Runes Appear:

  • Do not fear. A challenge is at hand.
  • Check position in spread: past (generational wound) or future (actionable now).
  • To integrate an obstacle is to accept that shadows come with light.

Five Ways to Deal with Obstacles

  1. Dissipate: Lessen its power. Make it less important.
  2. Release: "I release that which no longer serves me."
  3. Integrate: Lessons that cannot dissolve become part of you, like a scar.
  4. Transform: Transmute the experience. Hail it as a teacher.
  5. Accept: Some events require pain. Rely on your moral code when intuition fails.

Creating a Stop

The opposite of manifesting. Magick can inhibit or delay things already in motion.

Uses:

  • Stop a person from taking action
  • Delay or interrupt a process
  • Deflect a misfire or quell a brewing storm
  • Break communication patterns

Construction:

  1. Double Isa: Draw vertically and horizontally (equal-armed cross). Commands standstill in all directions.
  2. Inverted Ehwaz: Blocks forward momentum and movement.
  3. Dagaz: At apex of Ehwaz. Transforms unwanted energy.
  4. Circle: Enclose to contain energy.

Using the Stop

Circle as Containment: Scribe the circle first. Write within it what you wish to stop (contact from someone, rumors, bad dreams, an infection, a chain of events). Then cover with the stop sigil.

The Full Stop Charm:

Movement cease. Full stop.
Bring me peace. Full stop.
Do not proceed. Full stop.
Fulfill my need. Full stop.
Whisper no word. Full stop.
All goes unheard. Full stop.
Silence unbroken. Full stop.
My word has been spoken. Full stop.
And by my own will. Full stop.
This charm fulfill. Full stop.
